## 664. A new arena: Kalshi index markets. K-series family 1 protocol — the longshot bias in S&P and Nasdaq daily contracts (S9)

**No trial spent; N 1,525. Written and committed BEFORE any outcome is examined** (the download, `futuresres/kalshi/download.py`, saves
markets, results and hourly candles; nothing has been tabulated). The user (2026-10-17): search outside the Tradeify arena, per the
2026-10-16 brief (fresh ideas, more income, autonomous bots, no paid data). Kalshi (CFTC-regulated, US) lists daily S&P 500 range
(KXINX, 30 brackets), S&P above/below at the 4 PM close (KXINXU) and Nasdaq-100 range (KXNASDAQ100) contracts; settled history and hourly
yes bid / ask / trade candles are public and free since 2022; trading has a full API (an autonomous bot is possible); fees are quadratic,
taker ≈ 0.07 × p × (1 − p) a contract, rounded up per order. The best-documented bias in prediction markets is that **longshots are
overpriced**. Hypothesis: buying NO on cheap YES contracts earns more than it pays, after the spread and fees.

1. **Trade (fixed):** at the hourly candle ending 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 or 15:00 New York time on the settlement day, every contract of the
   event whose yes mid ((bid + ask) / 2, candle close) is in a bucket — (1, 5], (5, 10], (10, 20] cents — and whose quote is live (bid > 0,
   ask < $1, spread ≤ 10 cents): **buy NO at 1 − yes bid**, hold to settlement (payout $1 if the result is "no"). Fee: ceil(7 × q × (1 − q))
   cents per 100 contracts at NO price q. P&L per contract net of fee.
2. **Tests:** 3 series × 4 hours × 3 buckets = **36** (≈ 0.9 pass by chance at |t| > 1.96). Statistic per test: each day's mean net P&L
   per contract over its qualifying contracts; t over days; monthly t over month sums.
3. **Discovery: events settling before 2025-07-01. Sealed validation: 2025-07-01 → 2026-10-16** (asserted in code). **Carried:** t > 1.96,
   mean > 0, monthly t > 1.96 (as family 175). At most 5 carried, by t.
4. **Validation (once, sealed window):** CONFIRM if one-sided t > 1.645 on the daily series, beats ≥ 95% of a sign-randomisation placebo
   on the daily P&L (2,000 draws), and the posterior mean is positive (zero-mean prior shown too) — §119 adapted: a bet's return has no
   time-shift structure to shuffle, so the day-level sign flip is the null. Watchlist if net-positive but short of that (§133).
   Capacity is reported (qualifying contracts' hourly volume), since a bias in a thin book cannot be scaled.
5. **Caveats fixed now:** candle quotes are the hour's last quote, so fills at exactly that price are an assumption (to be checked
   live with small size); Kalshi's fee schedule and rules are as published today; the user's tax and account eligibility are the user's.

## 668. K-family 2 protocol: S&P contracts priced by our own model against Kalshi's quotes (S9)

**No trial spent; N 1,529. Written and committed BEFORE any model price is compared with any quote or outcome.** Model: at the candle
ending hh:00 New York (hh ∈ 10, 12, 14, 15), the S&P level S = the HistData S&P CFD minute close (corrected clock, `hd_grid`) at hh:00,
**plus the previous settlement day's basis** (Kalshi's recorded settlement value minus the CFD's 16:00 close that day — known before
today); daily volatility σ = root-mean-square over the previous 20 sessions of each session's realised 1-minute variance 09:30–16:00;
remaining variance σ² × (minutes to 16:00 / 390); zero drift, normal in log price. P(close ≥ K) = Φ(ln(S/K) / (σ√τ)); a range contract's
probability is the difference of its two bounds. **Trade** a contract when model − ask − fee(ask) > θ (buy YES) or (1 − model) − (1 − bid)
− fee(1 − bid) > θ (buy NO), quote filter as §664; hold to settlement. **Tests:** KXINXU (above/below at 4 PM) and KXINX (range) × 4 hours ×
θ ∈ {3¢, 6¢} = **16** (≈ 0.4 by chance). Statistic, carried rule and validation as §664 (discovery before 2025-07-01; **sealed 2025-07-01
→ 2026-09-30**, where the CFD minute data ends). The 2022 range-series naming (INX-…) and older above/below series are included where
candles exist. Caveat: the CFD tracks the cash index with a basis that moves within the day; the previous day's basis is an approximation.

## 669. K-family 2: our model does not beat Kalshi's S&P quotes — 0 of 16 carried (S9)

**N 1,529 (no trial).** `reports/k2_discovery.json` (module `kalshi/k2_model.py`). Inputs checked first: settlement-minus-CFD basis median
+0.24 points (day-to-day SD 2.9, against 25-point brackets); σ ≈ 0.6% a day. Discovery 2022-12 → 2025-06: where the model disagreed with the
quote by more than 3¢ / 6¢ after fees, trading its side lost in 12 of 16 cells (worst KXINXU 12:00 θ 6¢ −6.86¢, t −3.58); none carried.

them is paying for it. **Kalshi index markets: two families, no edge; the arena is set aside** unless a genuinely informed signal (one the
quotes cannot know) comes up. Its API remains the easiest route to a fully autonomous bot if one ever does.

## 670. A77 protocol: our two confirmed edges in CFD prop accounts with a static drawdown (The5ers High Stakes) (S9)

**No trial; N 1,529. Written and committed BEFORE any replay is run.** The user (2026-10-17) asked to search outside the Tradeify arena;
§131's objection was ~$500 fees, and cheap CFD accounts now exist. Our confirmed edges (NKD dollar-week, DAX-dollar) were measured on
HistData CFD prices — the instruments these firms list (JPN225, GER40). Rules as modelled (The5ers High Stakes, from its own page plus
third-party summaries; **to be confirmed by the user before any purchase**): Step 1 +10%, Step 2 +5%, each needing ≥ 3 profitable days
(closed profit ≥ 0.5% of the initial balance); **static maximum loss 10% of the initial balance**; daily loss 5%; no time limit, no
consistency rule; funded: 80% of profit above the initial balance, paid every 14 calendar days (10 sessions) from funding, the floor
staying at 90% of initial; no commission on indices; a failed account is re-bought (Classic prices: $5K $39, $10K $78; sizes scale
linearly, so per-dollar results are reported on $10K). One trade a day per traded market, in its current window with its deployed
side (A21 CFD paths; NKD 09:00–15:00 Tokyo, DAX 09:00–17:30 Frankfurt); costs: spread 2.2 bps (JPN225) / 0.6 bps (GER40) plus 1 bp
slippage a round trip. Position size: the window's 2021–24 daily SD = r% of the initial balance, r ∈ {1, 2, 3}; stop at s × r% (s ∈ {1,
2}; never more than the 5% daily limit or the room to the floor); take at k × stop, k ∈ {1, 2, none = hold to the window's end}; markets:
NKD, DAX, or both in one account (two trades a day) — 3 × 2 × 3 × 3 = **54 candidates** per account. Back-to-back accounts from every
start date, 84 sessions; net = 80% payouts − fees. **Chosen on 2021–24 starts** (mean net per $10K account); read once on 2025 starts and
2010–20 and with random sides (6 seeds). Reported: mean, median, P > 0, p10; payouts; evaluations bought; and the allocation ceiling
(three $5K + three $10K + one $25K + one $100K at once, New option). Not a trial (a computation on confirmed edges); a recommendation needs
the user's go-ahead on a second firm (§131, "multi-firm deferred").

## 672. K-family 3 protocol: Kalshi daily-high temperature contracts priced by the National Blend of Models (S9)

**No trial spent; N 1,529. Written and committed BEFORE any forecast is compared with any quote or outcome.** §669: an edge on Kalshi
needs information the quotes may not hold. The NWS National Blend of Models (NBM, text product NBS; free archive at the Iowa Environmental
Mesonet) gives each station's daytime maximum (TXN) and its spread (XND) — a probabilistic forecast built from ~30 models. Markets: daily
highs for **NYC (Central Park, KNYC), Chicago (Midway, KMDW), Miami (KMIA), Austin (KAUS), Los Angeles (KLAX), Denver (KDEN), Philadelphia
(KPHL)**, settled on the station's climate report (2°F brackets plus two tails; "greater than x" = ≥ x + 1, "less than x" = ≤ x − 1;
markets without a strike encoding are skipped). Fees quadratic, multiplier 1.

1. **Decision points:** T1 = the candle ending 10:00 New York on the day **before**, with that day's 07Z NBM run; T2 = 10:00 New York **on
   the day**, with that day's 07Z run (both runs are out by ~09Z). Forecast for local day D: TXN / XND valid D+1 00Z.
2. **Model:** high ~ Normal(μ, σ); P(bracket [a, b]) = Φ((b + 0.5 − μ)/σ) − Φ((a − 0.5 − μ)/σ). **Variants:** raw (μ = TXN, σ = max(XND, 1))
   and calibrated (per city: bias = mean(observed − TXN) and SD scale = SD(observed − TXN) / mean(XND), estimated on discovery days only,
   then fixed; observed = Kalshi's recorded settlement value).
3. **Trade:** model − ask − fee(ask) > θ → buy YES; (1 − model) − (1 − bid) − fee(1 − bid) > θ → buy NO; θ ∈ {5¢, 10¢}; quote filter as §664.
4. **Tests:** 2 times × 2 variants × 2 θ = **8**, cities pooled (per-city results reported, not tested); daily statistic = the day's mean
   net P&L per contract over all cities. **Discovery before 2025-07-01; sealed 2025-07-01 → 2026-10-16.** Carried / validation as §664.
5. **Year-round** (the user's rule): every day of the year trades; a result carried by one season will be reported as such.

re-fetch of 566 transient failures; NBM 07Z runs for 7 stations, ~39k rows each). Calibration (discovery days): biases within ±0.6°F; the

raw θ 5¢ +0.34¢ (t 0.46); **raw θ 10¢ +1.60¢ (t 1.81, monthly 1.91)** — positive in 6 of 7 cities (MIA +4.5¢, LAX +5.5¢, PHIL +1.8¢, AUS +1.5¢,
CHI +1.3¢, NY +1.1¢; DEN −4.9¢); calibrated θ 5¢ +0.24¢, θ 10¢ +1.28¢ (t 1.41). Below the carry bar (t > 1.96): **not validated**. Read: the

of history and the two venues' fees together take ~3.5¢ at even odds. **Sports:** football-data.co.uk publishes free match results and
pre-match / closing odds for ~22 European leagues since 2012/13, including **Pinnacle** (the sharp market; its de-margined price is the
standard fair-probability estimate) and **Bet365** (licensed in many US states). The documented strategy (Kaunitz, Zhong & Kreiner 2017)
is to bet where a soft bookmaker's odds exceed the sharp fair price.

1. **Rule:** fair p_i = (1 / PS_i) / Σ_j (1 / PS_j) from Pinnacle's pre-match 1X2 odds (proportional de-margining); value_i = B365_i × p_i − 1;
   **bet one unit on outcome i at Bet365's pre-match odds when value_i > θ** (both prices from the same pre-match snapshot, so the rule is
   executable at that time). Return B365_i − 1 if it wins, else −1.
2. **Tests:** θ ∈ {2%, 4%, 6%} × outcome ∈ {home, draw, away, any} = **12**. Statistic: each match date's mean return per bet; t over dates;
   monthly t. **Discovery: seasons 2012/13 → 2018/19. Sealed: 2019/20 → today** (asserted in code). Carried: t > 1.96, mean > 0, monthly t >
   1.96; validation once, §664.4's rule (one-sided t > 1.645, ≥ 95% sign-randomisation placebo, positive posterior).
3. **Reported beside validation:** closing-line value (Bet365 pre-match odds against Pinnacle's closing fair price, 2019/20 on), bets a
   season, and the stake capacity a typical US account would allow.
4. **Caveats fixed now:** Bet365's US odds can differ from the UK odds recorded; soft books limit accounts that win (a practical ceiling no
   backtest can show); legality depends on the user's state; football-data's pre-match snapshot is taken Friday / Tuesday afternoons, so
   later price moves are not seen.

## 677. S-family 1: Bet365 rarely beats Pinnacle's fair price, and when it does the bets earn nothing reliable — 0 of 12 (S10)

**N 1,532 (no trial).** `reports/s1_discovery.json` (module `sports/s1_value.py`; data: 22 leagues × 14 seasons, ~100k matches with both
prices). Discovery 2012/13 → 2018/19: the rule bet 4,788 times at θ 2% (of ~53,000 matches) — Bet365's pre-match odds are rarely above
Pinnacle's fair price; returns per bet −3.2% … +18% with |t| ≤ 0.81 in every cell (high variance, no signal). The Kaunitz result relied on
the best price across ~30 books; a single US-licensed book does not reproduce it. Sports value betting set aside.

## 678. K-family 4 protocol: Kalshi US gas-price contracts priced by the wholesale-to-retail lag (S10)

**No trial spent; N 1,532. Written and committed BEFORE any model price is compared with any quote or outcome.** Mechanism: US retail
gasoline follows wholesale (RBOB futures) with a lag of one to several weeks, faster up than down ("rockets and feathers"). Kalshi lists
daily (KXAAAGASD), weekly (KXAAAGASW) and monthly (KXAAAGASM) contracts on AAA's US average regular price ("strictly greater than $x on
date D"), each trading hundreds of thousands of contracts a day. Free inputs: Yahoo RB=F daily closes; EIA's weekly US regular retail price
(1990 →); AAA's level on each day from Kalshi's own recorded settlement values (daily series, 2023-09 →).

1. **Weekly model, fitted on EIA weekly 2010-01 → 2022-12 only (before any Kalshi gas market):** ΔR(t → t+1 week) = c + b0·ΔRB(week to t) +
   b1·ΔRB(week to t−1) + b2·ΔRB(week to t−2) + g·(R_t − RB_t − M_t), M_t the trailing 52-week mean of R − RB; up and down RBOB moves get
   separate b's (asymmetry); σ from residuals. Horizon h days: mean = weekly prediction × h/7, SD = σ·√(h/7); applied to AAA's level (AAA
   and EIA move together; their level gap cancels in changes).
2. **Daily model:** Δ(AAA, D−1 → D) = φ·(yesterday's AAA change) + (1 − φ)·(weekly prediction / 7); φ and σ_d fitted on **discovery days only**.
3. **Decision points (12:00 New York candle):** weekly — 6 and 3 days before settlement; monthly — 14 days before; daily — the day before.
   P(AAA_D > K) = 1 − Φ((K − μ)/sd). Trade as §668 (model − ask − fee > θ buys YES; the NO side likewise), θ ∈ {5¢, 10¢}.
4. **Tests:** weekly × 2 points × 2 θ + monthly × 1 × 2 + daily × 1 × 2 = **8**. Daily statistic over settlement dates; carried / validation
   as §664 (discovery before 2025-07-01; sealed 2025-07-01 → 2026-10-16). Year-round markets.

## 679. K-family 4: Kalshi's gas markets are too young to test — uninformative (S10)

**N 1,532 (no trial).** `reports/k4_discovery.json` (module `kalshi/k4_gas.py`). The weekly model fitted on EIA 2010–22 (656 weeks) is sensible
(RBOB pass-through ≈ 0.20 + 0.17 + 0.10 over three weeks on rises, a gap term −0.11, σ 4.4¢ a week), but before 2025-07 there are only 73 weekly
events (12:00 quote on ~half), 19 monthly (markets open 7 days before settlement, so the D−14 point never exists) and 24 daily (the daily
series is mostly 2026). Trades: weekly 13–21 days per cell, all negative (−6.5 … −12.3¢, |t| ≤ 1.8); monthly none; daily 2. **Uninformative**
— no split leaves enough history; set aside (a forward record would be the only way to test it).

## 680. S-family 2 protocol: NFL totals and game-day weather (S10)

**No trial spent; N 1,532. Written and committed BEFORE the data is examined.** nflverse (free, GitHub) records every NFL game since 1999
with the closing total and spread, roof type, temperature and wind. Mechanism: wind and cold lower passing efficiency and scoring; the
question is whether closing totals fully price it. **Bet the UNDER at −110** (win +0.909, loss −1, pushes void) in outdoor games
(roof "outdoors" or "open") with wind ≥ 10 / 15 / 20 mph, or temperature ≤ 25 / 35°F; and the OVER in dome / closed-roof games
(control-direction test) — **6 tests**. Statistic: per-week mean return over that week's bets; t over weeks. **Discovery: seasons 1999–2014.
Sealed: 2015–2025** (the 2026 season so far is excluded: forecasts at bet time vs recorded game-time weather, see caveat). Carried / validation as
§664.4. Caveats fixed now: nflverse weather is recorded at kickoff, while a bettor acts on a forecast hours earlier (forecasts of wind are good
but not perfect — an upper bound); closing totals are the hardest number to beat, so passing here is meaningful; legality is per state.

## 681. S-family 2: windy unders near-miss, cold unders lose — nothing carried (S10)

**N 1,532 (no trial).** `reports/s2_discovery.json` (module `sports/s2_nfl_weather.py`; nflverse games, 1999–2014). Under at wind ≥ 15 mph:
449 bets, **57.2% won, +9.3% a bet, weekly t 2.35, by-season t 1.52** (the carry rule needs both > 1.96); wind ≥ 20: 58.1%, +10.9%, t 1.74;
wind ≥ 10: +1.2%, t 0.0. **Unders in the cold lose:** temp ≤ 35°F 46.3%, −11.5% (t −2.22), ≤ 25°F 40.2%, −23.2% (t −2.19) — the market seems
to over-adjust totals down for cold. Dome overs: −0.1% (t 0.7).

## 682. S-family 2b protocol: one sealed look at windy unders and cold overs (S10)

**No trial spent; N 1,532. Written and committed BEFORE seasons 2015–2025 are read.** Suggested by §681 (the wind result is also the
published hypothesis; the cold result is its mirror), so tested only on data §681 did not use: **under at wind ≥ 15 mph; over at temp ≤ 35°F;
over at temp ≤ 25°F** (outdoor / open roof; −110; pushes void) — **3 tests**, each judged alone and reported against 3. Sealed seasons
2015–2025, read once; CONFIRM per §664.4 (one-sided weekly t > 1.645, ≥ 95% sign-randomisation placebo on weekly returns, positive posterior);
watchlist if net-positive. Season-by-season results reported.

## 683. S-family 2b: windy NFL unders hold out of sample but are too sparse to confirm — WATCHLIST; cold overs REJECT (S10)

**3 trials (t01533–t01535); N 1,535.** `reports/s2b_validation.json`. Sealed seasons 2015–2025: **under at wind ≥ 15 mph — 225 bets, 56.4% won,
+7.8% a bet** (discovery 57.2%, +9.3%), but weekly t 0.53, placebo 70% → **WATCHLIST** (positive in 6 of 11 seasons). Over at ≤ 35°F −6.7% a
bet, over at ≤ 25°F −20.2% → REJECT (both sides of cold totals lose — the vig, not a mispricing). Read: the published wind effect persists
at ~57% over 26 seasons, but it is ~20 bets a season — at $100 a bet about +$150 a season. Too small to be an income stream.

## 684. A78 protocol: the staking game in a crypto prop with a static floor and on-demand payouts (Breakout Classic 1-step) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE any game is solved or replayed.** The user (2026-10-17): other funded programmes — someone
else's capital with rules we can model. Tradeify's game pays at zero edge through its rules; this asks whether Breakout's (Kraken-owned crypto
prop) does too. Rules as modelled (Kraken's comparison page and third-party reviews; **to be confirmed by the user at checkout**): one-step
target +10%; **static** maximum loss 6% of the starting balance; daily loss 3% of the day's starting balance; no time limit, no minimum days,
no consistency rule; funded: **80% of any profit above the starting balance, withdrawable on demand**, floor stays at −6%; fee ≈ 1% of the
account ($100 per $10K; $100K $800–999); fee refund on the first payout NOT assumed; trading fee assumed 0.05% of notional a side (taker)
plus 0.02% slippage; leverage ≤ 5× (BTC).
1. **The game (A01's method):** balance in 0.25% steps; each day one bracket on BTC — stop L ≤ 3% of the account (daily limit), take W from
   a menu up to the target; win probability at zero edge p = (L − c)/(W + L) with c the round-trip cost of the notional needed for that
   stop at a fixed stop distance in price; evaluation value = P(pass within H days) and funded value = E[80% of withdrawals within H days];
   EV per attempt = P(pass) × funded value − fee. H = 84 and 252 days; reported per $10K.
2. **Replay check:** the solved policy on real BTC-USD hourly paths (free Coinbase/Binance data), entry at 00:00 UTC, the bracket by the
   policy, out at 23:00 UTC, **sides random** (zero edge, 6 seeds) — the game's EV must survive real paths and costs.
3. **Read:** EV per attempt and per $10K a month, P(pass), payouts per funded account, evaluations bought, the cash low point; a positive
   zero-edge EV that survives the replay makes this a candidate income stream needing no edge (as Tradeify), subject to the user's checks
   (US eligibility, current fees, any prohibited-strategy clause). Not a trial (no edge is tested).

## 685. A78: Breakout's structure is worth ~+0.6% an attempt in the idealised game but loses on real BTC paths — not an income stream as modelled (S10)

**No trial.** `reports/a78_crypto_prop.json` (modules `reporting/a78_crypto_prop.py`, `a78_btc_data.py`; Coinbase BTC-USD hourly 2018-01 →
2026-10, 3,206 days). Solved game (zero edge, costs priced): P(pass) 35.7%, funded value 4.49% of the account, **EV +0.60% an attempt**
(+$60 per $10K) — the best play risks the full 3% daily limit for the whole 10% target, and once funded risks 0.5% for 10%. (A first solve
let the policy skip trading at long horizons — waiting ties betting at zero edge — and was corrected to A01's always-trade rule.) **Replay,
random sides (6 seeds), per $10K:** out at 23:00 UTC daily — 84 days −$145 (P > 0 5%), 252 days −$204 (14%); held to take or stop (crypto
trades around the clock; added, disclosed; funding 0.03% a day) — 84 days −$101 (10%), 252 days −$64 (22%, p90 +$463). Why: the coin game
ignores time — its long-odds brackets (take 20× the stop) need 60% BTC moves, so trades mostly end at the window's close while costs and
funding accrue. A rough check with brackets that resolve in days: ~+0.8% gross minus ~0.5–0.7% costs ≈ zero. **The fee refund on the first
payout (reported by some sources, denied by others) is what would make it positive (+~0.4% an attempt); without it, not worth doing.**
Static-floor, on-demand programmes are the right shape; Breakout's fee (1% of the account) and crypto's costs leave too little.

report only a success. nflverse games (closing spread, rest days, division flag, weekday, kickoff time). Bets at −110 against the closing
spread (pushes void); a home cover = home margin > spread_line (positive spread_line = home favoured). **Tests (each a published idea):**
(1) home underdogs; (2) the team with ≥ 3 more days of rest (e.g. off a bye); (3) Thursday games — the home team; (4) divisional underdogs;
(5) underdogs of 10+ points; (6) the under in prime time (kickoff ≥ 19:00 Eastern, any day) — **6 tests**. Statistic: weekly mean return; t
over weeks; season t. **Discovery seasons 1999–2014; sealed 2015–2025.** Carried: t > 1.96, mean > 0, season t > 1.96; validation once per
§664.4. Caveat: closing lines are the hardest to beat; a bettor gets an earlier line.

## 688. K-family 5 protocol: Kalshi weekly TSA screenings priced by a nowcast from the days already published (S10)

**No trial spent; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE any market is downloaded or any nowcast compared with a quote.** KXTSAW (since
2021-07): "weekly average TSA screenings above X for the week ending Sunday"; opens Monday 10:00 New York, trades to Sunday 23:59. TSA publishes
each day's count the next morning (data: tsa.gov's yearly tables via the Internet Archive, 2019-01-01 → 2026-10-15, complete). Mechanism: by
mid-week several of the seven days are public; the question is whether quotes fully use them.
1. **Nowcast at 12:00 New York on day t** (days through t−1 known, k = number known this week): each unknown day = the same weekday 364 days
   earlier × r, r = (sum of the known days) / (sum of their 364-day-earlier days); with k = 0, r from the previous complete week. Weekly
   average μ = (known + forecast)/7. Error: Normal with SD = σ_k × μ, σ_k = SD of (actual − nowcast)/actual over discovery weeks for each k.
2. **Trade:** P(average > X) = 1 − Φ((X − μ)/(σ_k μ)); buy YES / NO when the edge over the ask after fee > θ, θ ∈ {5¢, 10¢}; quote filter as §664.
3. **Decision days:** Tuesday (k = 1), Thursday (k = 3), Saturday (k = 5) — **6 tests**. Statistic: weekly mean net per contract; t over weeks;
   monthly t. **Discovery: weeks ending before 2025-07-01; sealed: 2025-07-01 → 2026-10-11.** Carried / validation as §664.4.

364-day-ratio nowcast's error (discovery weeks, 2020 included) is wide: SD 7.6% with Monday known, 6.6% with three days, 2.8% with five. Trades

~50 weeks)** — none near the bar. The market already reads the published days at least as well as a simple seasonal ratio.

## 690. K-family 6 protocol: Kalshi EUR/USD and USD/JPY 10:00 ranges priced by our own model (S10)

**No trial spent; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE any model price is compared with any quote or outcome.** KXEURUSD / KXUSDJPY
(since 2022-08): each day's range brackets on the rate at 10:00 New York; markets open 10:00 the day before. Model as §668 with the FX minute
grid (HistData, corrected clock, `hd_grid`): level = the grid's last close at the decision minute plus the previous settlement's basis
(Kalshi's recorded value − the grid at 10:00 that day); σ = RMS over the previous 20 days of the 24-hour realised 1-minute variance, scaled to
the time left; zero drift, normal in log price; a bracket's probability = difference of its bounds. **Decision points:** 12:00 the day before
(22 h left), 16:00 the day before (18 h), 08:00 on the day (2 h); θ ∈ {3¢, 6¢}; trade as §668 — 2 pairs × 3 points × 2 θ = **12 tests**.
**Discovery before 2025-07-01; sealed 2025-07-01 → 2026-09-30** (the minute data's end). Carried / validation as §664.4.

a live quote by more than θ on only 0–51 days per cell before 2025-07 (the books are thin and wide: the quote filter removes most hours); every
cell |t| < 1, means −10.6¢ … +6.0¢. Uninformative-to-null. **WTI (KXWTI) is not run:** the same model on oil has only 18 months of free minute

## 692. A new structural arena: Kalshi's Liquidity Incentive Program. A79 protocol — completing thin order books (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE the forward sampler runs.** Kalshi pays each incentivised market's pool ($1–1,000 a market a
day; ~6,800 active programmes, ≈ $235,000 a day in total on 2026-10-17, from the public `incentive_programs` API) to resting orders: snapshots
every second; a snapshot counts only if resting size reaches the **target (usually 1,000 contracts) on both the yes and the no side**; on each
side an order's weight is its size × (discount factor ^ ticks below the reference price, the level where cumulative size reaches target/5),
shares are normalised per side, a snapshot is worth at most 2.0, payout = period score × reward × (counted snapshots / all snapshots). US
members eligible. A first snapshot of 300 active markets (`reports/lip_probe.json`): 87% of books already meet the target on both sides; in
the rest one side is nearly empty — often the long-shot side of a contract far from the money (state daily gas, Rotten Tomatoes, mentions).
**Strategy (fixed now):** for each active programme (≥ 12 h long) whose yes or no side is below target, post the missing side's target size at
**1¢** (the lowest price: loss if filled and wrong ≤ 1¢ a contract; filled only if someone sells near-certain outcomes below 1¢'s odds). **Forward
measurement (no money):** sample every active programme's book every 15 minutes for 3 hours (local machine only); for each, the share this order
would earn per side and whether the snapshot would then count; estimated $ a day per market and per $ of collateral; persistence of the thin side
across samples. **Read:** it is a candidate income stream if the estimated earnings stay large across samples; the live check (a few markets,
real orders, small size, the user's go-ahead) comes after. Risks named now: other quoters doing the same (shares fall), programme changes or
end (sources say January 2027), Kalshi treating it as abusive (its rules score size × distance and say nothing against far orders).

## 693. A79: completing thin books in Kalshi's liquidity programme measures as a large, persistent gap — a live test is the next step (S10)

**No trial (a measurement of the present, not an edge test).** `reports/lip_sampler.jsonl` (22 sweeps, two independent random samples of
~500 active programmes — the afternoon run continued through the planned shutdown while a resumed run drew a fresh 500; split in
`kalshi/lip_summary.py`), 2026-10-17 20:59Z → 2026-10-18 00:50Z. Posting the target size at 1¢ on every side below target would have earned
(by the published scoring, given every other resting order seen): **sample A $1,578 a day (range $1,305–2,120) on $620 of collateral; sample B
$1,380 a day ($1,063–1,746) on $554**; ~10–12% of sampled programmes are thin at any sweep; **96% / 90% of thin sides are still thin 15 minutes
later**; the top 10 markets carry a third of the total; leading series: KXRAIN, KXRT (Rotten Tomatoes), state daily / weekly gas (KXAAAGASD…),
mentions and weekly event markets. Scaled to all ~6,700 programmes: **~$18,500–21,600 a day — an upper bound** (no copycats, payout exactly
as written). The official terms (CFTC filing, 2026-07-15) set no price restriction on qualifying bids and **exclude members with a Market
Maker Agreement** — the likeliest reason the gap persists. **Caveats:** estimates, not payouts — Kalshi actually paying as written is
untested; copycats split a side's share; the programme ends by 2027-01-01 at the latest and may end any time; Kalshi may revoke a participant
judged "inconsistent with the purpose of the Program"; a filled 1¢ bid loses its 1¢ if the long shot does not happen (≤ $10 a market). **Next:
a small live test** (≈10 persistent thin markets, 1,000 contracts at 1¢ each, ~$100 of collateral, 3–5 days) on the user's go-ahead and
account; payouts compared with these estimates before any scale-up.

## 694. The Kalshi liquidity bot: built, tested, running dry on the droplet; live test waits for the user's key (S10)

**No trial.** The user (2026-10-17): use the droplet so it runs 24/7; **only programmes of two days or less** at first (faster payouts,
faster scaling). Kalshi's terms (help centre): estimated earnings show per market in the app's Rewards popover; paid credits under Rewards and
Account → Activity; scoring happens after a programme ends and payment follows in a later run; programme periods range from 15 minutes to
weeks (~935 under a day, ~910 of 1–2 days among 6,800 active); no per-account cap is set. `kalshi_lip/` (separate from the futures bot):
`kalshi_api.py` (Ed25519 / RSA-PSS request signing, V2 orders — single book, bid = yes, ask = no, price always the YES price — batch order
books), `lip_bot.py` (every 5 minutes: short programmes → books → sides whose OTHER traders' size is below target → our target-size bid at 1¢,
post-only, expiring at the programme's end; best 10 markets by estimated $ per $ of collateral within $150; cancels sides no longer needed;
accrues an estimate from the published scoring; daily Discord summary; first live order read back and verified or everything is cancelled;
STOP file kill switch). A unit test caught one scoring error (an order at a qualifying price level counts in full) — fixed. **Deployed in
MODE=dry 2026-10-18 01:06Z** (`kalshi-lip.service`, /opt/kalshi-lip, MemoryMax 150M; Discord via the futures bot's token, read-only).
First loops: ~1,826 short programmes, ~520 with a thin side; its chosen 10 would hold ~$96 of collateral for an estimated ~$9,000 a day,
mostly **Miami hourly temperature markets ($100 an hour each, long-shot side empty)** — plausible by the rules, unproven until paid.

## 695. The live test failed: thin sides are thin because informed sellers fill any 1¢ bid at once — bot stopped, ~$36 at risk (S10)

**No trial.** Live 2026-10-18 01:46–01:57Z ($150 funded; programmes ≤ 2 days). Sequence: (1) orders defaulted to exchange shard 0 →
"market not found" on a LigaPro match (sports shard 3) — fixed by routing per market; (2) **"post only cross" on many thin sides**: where
the opposite side bids 99¢, a 1¢ bid crosses, so those sides can never rest — my sampler (§692–693) had counted them as earnable, inflating
its estimates; fixed by requiring the opposite best bid < 99¢; (3) the first order's read-back ran before Kalshi listed it, the safety stop
did not cancel an order it had not yet recorded, and systemd restarted the bot — three loops, two orphan orders (cancelled), and a **LigaPro
in-play match bid filled 300 contracts at 1¢ ($3)**; fixed (retry + client-id match, record before verify, no restart on a safety stop,
sports / match markets excluded); (4) the corrected bot placed 10 verified 1¢ bids on state daily gas markets (settling the next day) and
**4 were filled within seconds** (≈2,800 contracts, ≈$33): someone sells the long shot to any 1¢ bid in markets whose outcome is nearly
known. Each fill re-opens the side, so the bot would re-post and bleed ~$30–40 every loop — **stopped, disabled and all orders cancelled**.
Positions: five long shots at 1¢ (≈$36.26 exposure; cash $113.74) — expected to expire worthless. **Read:** the "gap" is not free money:
completable thin sides stay thin because resting there is filled by better-informed traders almost at once, so the reward accrues for
seconds while each fill costs ~1¢ a contract. Short programmes (near resolution) are the worst case. The live test did its job: it found
what no snapshot could. Whether longer programmes (outcome still uncertain, slower informed flow) behave differently is an open question;
not pursued without the user's decision.

## 696. A80 protocol: do longer liquidity programmes escape the adverse fills? — measured from public trades, no money (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE the measurement runs.** The user (2026-10-18): test longer programmes. Programmes lasting
**≥ 6 days with ≥ 1 day left** (outcome further from known). For each: the book now; a side is **completable** if other traders' resting size
is below target AND the opposite best bid is < 99¢ (so a 1¢ bid can rest). **Reward:** our share (scoring as §692, with the price-level rule
of §694) × the programme's reward rate. **Fills:** the public trades of the last 72 hours (`GET /markets/trades`) at the 1¢ level on that
side (taker selling the long shot: yes-price 1¢ with taker side no for a yes bid; yes-price 99¢ with taker side yes for a no bid); we would
have been filled only after the size already resting at 1¢ ahead of us — fills to us = max(0, traded − ahead), per day. **Cost of a fill:**
1¢ a contract (the long shot assumed to lose — informed sellers). **Net a day = reward − fills × $0.01.** Reported: markets measured, how
many net-positive, total net a day per $ of collateral, and by series; the same computed for programmes ≤ 2 days as the control (it must
show the failure §695 saw). **Read:** a candidate only if net stays clearly positive with the control behaving as observed live; then a
forward check over days before any money.

## 697. A80: historical trades cannot measure the fill risk — the control fails, so the longer-programme question stays open (S10)

**No trial.** `reports/a80_lip_long.json` (module `kalshi/a80_lip_long.py`). Long programmes (≥ 6 days, ≥ 1 day left): 3,357 active, 71 with a
completable thin side; reward $629/day, fill cost from 72 h of 1¢ trades $160/day, **net +$469/day** on $985 of collateral, 59 of 71 positive
(KXBA, KXYTVIEWSW, KXDPZ lead; 52 of 71 show no 1¢ fills in 72 h). **Control (≤ 2 days): net +$8,869/day, 145 of 150 positive — but live
(§695) 4 of 10 such bids were filled within seconds.** The method fails its control: before anyone bid 1¢ there was little to trade against,
so past trades miss the sellers who wait for a bid. Fill risk is created by posting and can only be measured by posting. The longer-programme
question is therefore unanswered by public data; the only test is a small live probe (user's decision).

## 698. A81 protocol: a small live probe of longer liquidity programmes (user's go-ahead) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE the probe starts.** The only way to measure fill risk (§697). Programmes **≥ 6 days long
with ≥ 1 day left**; completable thin sides (others below target, opposite best bid < 99¢); 1,000-contract bids at 1¢; **at most 5 markets
and $50 of collateral**; sports / match markets excluded; **a side that has been filled is never re-posted**; every fill logged and posted to
Discord; **hard stop if fill cost exceeds $20** (cancel all, exit, no restart). Run 24–48 hours. Read: fills per market per day against the
break-even of ~1 full fill a day (§697 table); the rewards estimate in each market's Kalshi popover; then, once a programme ends, the paid
credit against the estimate. Decision after: scale within the fill rate observed, or close the arena.

week ending today) — the near-certain case again — so a **market-close condition was added: the market must close ≥ 3 days ahead**
(`MIN_MARKET_DAYS`). Live from 2026-10-18 02:10Z: 1,000 at 1¢ on KXWEEKSNUM1-26DEC26-TAYL-5 (no), KXAAAGASMINM-26OCT31-4.30 (no),
KXSUPERBOWLHEADLINE-27-EDS (yes), KXWNBAFINALSMVP-26-THAYES15 (yes), KXTRUMPSAYMONTH-26NOV01-NEWS (no); $50 collateral; all five verified
resting; **no fill on placement** (the short gas markets filled within seconds). Estimated reward ~$30 a day. Stop rule $20 of fill cost.

## 700. The user's canary idea, live: 1-contract probes find the waiting sellers; long probe capped at 8-day periods (S10)

**No trial.** The user (2026-10-18): payouts follow each programme *period* (the held markets' periods: 7, 7 and 14 days; first ends 10-21), so
the long probe's periods are capped at **8 days** for roughly weekly payouts; and the user's idea — **test a market with a 1-contract order
before committing**. The sellers who filled the gas bids (§695) were not resting (a resting seller would have made our bid cross); they arrive
after a bid appears, so they are invisible in the book but a canary flushes them for 1¢. Built as a **separate instance** (`kalshi-lip-short`,
own env / state / log / stop file; short programmes ≤ 2 days, no market-close condition, ≤ 5 markets, $50, **stop at $10 of fills**):
each new side gets **1 contract, then 100, then the full size**, a loop (5 min) apart; a fill at any step drops that side for good.
Fixes on the way: the order check now looks an order up by id and accepts "executed" (a canary filled within seconds is a valid order and a
detected seller); fills are rebuilt each loop from Kalshi's records using the fill's `outcome_side` (an earlier guess from side/action read a
1¢ NO fill as YES at 99¢) and matched to each instance's own order ids. **First results: Miami hourly temperature canaries were filled
within seconds (3 of the first ~6, 1 contract each, 3¢ in all); state daily gas canaries are being tried; the long probe: no fills.**

passed), **🟠 large fill** (a fill costing ≥ $5 — a real loss), **🔴 stopped** (fill limit, failed check or kill switch). Dropped: every
small (canary) fill — counted in the daily results instead — and start messages on routine restarts (only a fresh start posts). Rewards now
accrue in the estimate only while every needed side holds its full size (a canary alone completes nothing).

## 702. Seven improvements to both liquidity bots (the user: apply all now) (S10)

**No trial.** Deployed 2026-10-18 03:13Z to `kalshi-lip` and `kalshi-lip-short`. (1) **Stay unless it stops paying** — a held order is kept
while its projected reward to the period end (share now × reward rate × time left) is ≥ $1, instead of leaving the moment another trader
completes the side; (2) **re-entry skips the canary** for a side that passed it today; (3) **series blacklist** — a series whose canaries are
swept twice in a day is skipped for the rest of the day; (4) **enter only if the projected reward to the period end is ≥ $3** (Kalshi pays
nothing under $1 a period; the New Jersey order rested 15 minutes and showed $0.00); (5) **price 1–3¢** and (6) **size = the shortfall or the
full target**, per side, whichever maximises projected reward − worst-case fill cost (size × price) — e.g. with 700 resting at 2¢, a 1,000
bid at 3¢ takes the whole side under the scoring (bids below the target cut-off do not qualify); (7) **canary steps wait a real 5 minutes by
the clock**. Unit-checked and dry-run on both configurations first. A dry check showed most long programmes (6–8 days) sit on markets closing
within 3 days, so the long probe currently has few candidates (the market-close rule is doing its job).

## 704. Held orders are judged with their fill risk; one order pinned at the user's request (S10)

**No trial.** The user asked why the short bot posted a full order at 22:09 CDT for a period ending 22:59 (Georgia daily gas): it was the old
step-up logic (§702 deployed 22:13); there is no minimum holding time — rewards accrue per one-second snapshot, with Kalshi's $1 minimum per
period. It exposed a flaw in §702: a held order was valued as risk-free to keep, but a resting order keeps its fill risk, and short markets'
final stretch is when informed sellers are most active. **Now a held order is valued like a new one — projected reward to the period end minus
the worst-case fill cost** — and leaves when that turns negative (with 50 minutes left on a $100 / 16 h pool, a 1,000 at 1¢ is worth −$7.40;
with 10 hours left +$21). **Pinned at the user's request** (`PIN_KEYS`): KXAAAGASDGA-26OCT18-3.7750 yes, 1,000 at 1¢, kept to its period end
(22:59 CDT) to watch what happens.

## 708. A82 protocol: the other side — do traders who sell long shots near settlement win often enough? (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE any trade is downloaded.** The user (2026-10-17): if completing thin books fails, could a
bot take the other side — fill the long-shot bids others rest (as was done to ours), presumably knowing the outcome? A taker who sells a
long shot at p (1–3¢) — i.e. buys the favourite at 100 − p — keeps p a contract if the favourite wins and loses 100 − p if it does not; the
taker fee is ≈ 0.07 × p × (1 − p) a contract (rounded up per order). Break-even: the favourite must win more than ≈ (100 − p + fee)/100
of the time (≈ 99.3% at 1¢).
1. **Markets:** settled events of the last 45 days in the short series the bots met — state daily gas (every KXAAAGASD… series), Miami hourly
   temperature (KXTEMPMIAH), weekly executive orders (KXEOWEEK) — plus daily highs (KXHIGH… cities) as a wider check.
2. **Trades:** Kalshi's public trades (taker side, price, size, time) on every market; a **long-shot sale** = the taker buys the favourite at
   ≥ 97¢ (yes at ≥ 97¢, or no at ≥ 97¢).
3. **Read:** per series group, per price (97 / 98 / 99¢ for the favourite) and per time left to the market's close (≤ 1 h, 1–6 h, 6–24 h,
   > 24 h): contracts, favourite win rate (Wilson 95% interval), and the takers' net P&L per contract after fees. **A strategy candidate only
   where the win rate's lower bound clears break-even with room**; a positive aggregate dominated by one rare loss is reported as such.
   No orders are placed; this measures what others earned.

long-shot sales, 35.1M contracts; a first pass hit Kalshi's trade-endpoint rate limit and was completed by a slower second pass). Takers who

at every price (97¢ +2.08¢, 98¢ +1.12¢, 99¢ +0.45¢) and every time-to-close**; Miami hourly +0.49¢ but −1.41¢ at 97¢; daily highs +0.05¢;
executive orders +1.32¢ (16 markets). **Gas losses cluster: 40 of 45 days positive (median +$4,525), worst day 2026-10-14 −$41,314 (favourite
lost in 30 of 709 markets), then −$10,169, −$7,600, −$6,116, −$5,029.** Capital-heavy: ~99¢ tied up per contract to earn ~0.56¢. A candidate

## 710. A83 protocol: selling long shots in state daily gas only when the outcome is safely decided (S10)

**No trial; N 1,535. Written and committed BEFORE the market details are fetched or any rule is scored.** The user (2026-10-18): test the edge
behind §709. Data: the A82 trades (state daily gas, every KXAAAGASD… series, 45 days); each market's strike and its settled AAA value
(re-fetched); Yahoo RB=F daily closes (wholesale gasoline). For a long-shot sale (we buy the favourite at 97–99¢, as the historical taker did)
in market (state s, date D, strike K) at time t: **L** = the state's latest settled AAA value before D (the price already known); **cushion** =
how far the favourite side is from losing, in cents: (K − L) when the favourite is "not above K", (L − K) when it is "above K"; **wholesale
move** = |RB=F's last close before t − the close two trading days earlier| in ¢/gal. **Rule: take the sale only if cushion ≥ X and wholesale
move ≤ Y**, X ∈ {2, 4, 6}¢, Y ∈ {3, 6, ∞}¢ — 9 rules. Each scored as if we had been the taker of every qualifying historical sale (an upper
bound on capacity: we could not have taken them all). **Chosen on the first 30 days by mean daily net P&L per $ of capital (99¢ a contract
tied up until settlement); read once on the last 15 days.** Reported for each: net per contract after fees, days positive, worst day,
contracts a day, and the same for "take everything" (the §709 baseline). **Candidate only if, on the last 15 days, the chosen rule is positive,
beats the baseline per contract, and its worst day is smaller than the baseline's.** The 45-day history is short; a pass means a small live
trial, not scale.

## 711. A83: the chosen rule fails — selected on 2 days; second-look protocol with a minimum sample (S10)

**No trial.** `reports/a83_rule.json` (modules `kalshi/a83_meta.py`, `a83_rule.py`; 65,821 long-shot sales, 1,261 events, all "above K"
markets with settled values). **The wholesale filter (|RB=F 2-day move| ≤ 3¢ or 6¢) almost never passes** — gasoline futures usually move more —
so §710's selection by return per capital picked "cushion ≥ 2¢, move ≤ 3¢", which **traded on 2 of 30 discovery days**; on validation it lost
**−2.53¢ a contract (worst day −$41,359)** against the baseline's +0.32¢ (worst −$41,314) → **not a candidate**. The protocol's flaw: no minimum
sample. Discovery also shows **"cushion ≥ 6¢, any move": +1.17¢ a contract, 22 of 22 days positive, worst day +$21**, ~25,800 contracts a day.
**A83b protocol (second look, written BEFORE its validation numbers are read):** the same 9 rules on the same discovery days, chosen by return
per capital **among rules trading on ≥ 15 discovery days** (which picks cushion ≥ 6¢, any move); read once on the 15 validation days; same
candidate test as §710. Reported as a second look at the validation window (two looks; the first failed).

## 712. A83b (second look): "cushion ≥ 6¢" passes on the validation days — a thin, real candidate (S10)

**No trial.** `reports/a83b_rule.json`. Chosen among rules trading on ≥ 15 discovery days: **cushion ≥ 6¢, any wholesale move**. Validation
(15 days, the second look at this window — the first rule failed, §711): **+0.38¢ a contract after fees (+0.380% of capital per turn), 12 of 14
days positive, worst day −$2,085** — against "take everything" +0.32¢, worst −$41,314. Candidate test met (positive, better per contract,
far smaller worst day). Discovery: +1.17¢, 22/22 days. Read: selling a long shot only when the state's last settled AAA price is ≥ 6¢ on the
favourite's side of the strike avoids the moving days that made the October 14 loss; the edge is thin (~0.4–1.2¢ a contract) and the worst
validation day was ~15 typical days' profit. Capacity: ~25,000–37,000 such contracts a day were sold by all takers together. Caveats: 45 days
of history, two looks at the validation window, and execution (we would have to reach those bids first, competing with the takers who did).

3. **Trade:** base rate − ask − fee > θ buys Yes; (1 − base rate) − (1 − bid) − fee > θ buys No; θ ∈ {5¢, 10¢, 15¢} — **3 tests**.

hour after the market opened: θ 5¢ +3.66¢ a contract (64 events, 352 contracts, t 1.07); **θ 10¢ +6.76¢ (61 events, 283 contracts, t 1.78)**;
θ 15¢ +6.45¢ (t 1.63). The first, incomplete pass had θ 10¢ at t 2.04 — it fell below the bar once the missing events were in, so the rule was
judged on the complete data before any sealed look. **Nothing carried; no validation.** Even if real, ~300 qualifying contracts in ten months is
not an income stream. Closed.

## 722. Screen: Polymarket US's liquidity and deposit incentives fail (S10)

**No trial.** Polymarket US runs a Liquidity Incentive Program (docs.polymarket.us/incentives/liquidity), but it scores each order by
**discount factor ^ ticks from the best price** (often 0.30 a tick) with target sizes and an optional max spread around the midpoint — so only
quotes at or near the best price earn: professional market-making in deep sports books against sharp flow (the adverse selection of §695 at
the touch). The thin-side 1¢ trick of §692 does not apply. Its deposit / refer-a-friend / deposit-and-trading credits ($25 … $250, non-
withdrawable trading credits) are one-off bonuses — the category the user excluded. **Both fail the screen; not built.**

(NKD + FDXM) −$2,650 against ≈ −$100 ± ~$3,300 (z ≈ −0.8). With ≈ +$100–200 of edge a ticket against ≈ ±$1,000 of noise, ~150–200 tickets a

## 725. Screen: ForecastEx Liquidity Incentive Program (via IBKR) — the pool is too small; out (S10)

**No trial.** Read-only API access to the user's IBKR paper account works (TWS on the user's PC, 192.168.1.203:7497); ForecastEx contracts,
live quotes and depth come through. The terms (NTM 2026-221, effective 2026-09-01): one snapshot a second; only orders AT the best price score;
a snapshot counts only if both sides hold the target size (200-5,000) at the best price; pro-rata share of a per-product daily pool
= 3-day volume / 3,000 (10 bp of $1 notional). The public daily reports (forecastex-public-data S3, liquidity_rewards/, 45 days 09-04 to
10-18) give the whole exchange's pool: **mean $185/day, median $152, min $35, max $655; $8,345 in total**, for all participants combined.
The largest products are FFDEC $53/day, FES $39, FNQ $19, HORC $17. Even a large share is a few tens of $/day, and earning it means
resting size at the best price, which carries the informed-fill exposure that sank the Kalshi short LIP (§713). Customer eligibility also
depends on IBKR having arranged pass-through (unverified). Fails the size screen; closed.

## 726. F-family 1 protocol — ForecastEx daily-high contracts settle on Weather Underground, not NWS: is YES overpriced? (S10)

**No trial spent. Written and committed BEFORE any ForecastEx price is compared with any outcome.** Screen (§717 criterion): a
**structural** edge — a settlement-rule difference between venues. ForecastEx's daily-high contracts ("will the high exceed X?") resolve on
the highest value in Weather Underground's Daily Observations table (mostly hourly METARs); Kalshi's resolve on the NWS climate report
(continuous data). The no-price screen `forecastex/f0_settle.py` (ForecastEx settlements vs Kalshi's `expiration_value`, same stations:
LAX, Midway, Austin-Bergstrom, Miami, Philadelphia; Feb-Sep 2026, 231-243 days each) finds the NWS high **above** ForecastEx's bracket on
55-68% of days (mostly by 1 F, sometimes 2-3 F), below it on 0-4 days. Hypothesis: traders anchor ForecastEx to NWS-based forecasts and
Kalshi, so ForecastEx YES is overpriced. Why might it be untaken? ForecastEx is a small, mostly retail IBKR venue; against it, LA trades
~70M contracts since February and retained market makers quote temperatures, so the gap may be priced in. That is what this tests.
Data: every ForecastEx trade (`pairs/`, public S3, via `forecastex/download.py`); settlements from `prices/`.
1. **Trade (fixed):** every trade (pair) in UHLAX, UHMDW, UHAUS, UHMIA, UHPHL with yes price in [0.10, 0.90]: **buy NO at the pair's NO
   price + 1¢ slippage**, pay the 1¢ ForecastEx fee, hold to settlement ($1 if NO). The pair has no aggressor flag, so being the NO side
   at that price is an assumption; the 1¢ is the allowance for it.
2. **Tests:** 5 cities × 2 windows (pair time in the city's local time: (a) before 10:00 on the contract date, incl. the day before;
   (b) 10:00-16:00 on the contract date) = **10** (≈ 0.25 pass by chance). Statistic: each contract-date's quantity-weighted mean net per
   contract; t over dates.
3. **Discovery: contract dates before 2026-07-01. Sealed validation: 2026-07-01 → 2026-10-17** (asserted in code). **Carried:** t > 1.96,
   mean > 0, positive in ≥ 4 of the 5 discovery months (Feb-Jun; monthly t is meaningless over 5 months). At most 3 carried, by t.
4. **Validation (once, sealed):** as §664.4 (one-sided t > 1.645 over dates; ≥ 95% of a 2,000-draw date-level sign-flip placebo;
   positive posterior, zero-mean prior shown). Watchlist if net-positive but short of that (§133). Capacity: qualifying contracts a day.
5. **Caveats fixed now:** fills at trade prices are an assumption to be checked live via IBKR quotes (read-only API works, §725) before
   any money; the fee is ForecastEx's published 1¢ (IBKR commission, if any, to be confirmed); trading eligibility is the user's.

## 727. F-family 1: the settlement gap is priced in — 1 of 10 carried, rejected on sealed data (S10)

**N 1,536 (one trial, t01536).** `reports/f1_discovery.json`, `reports/f1_validation.json` (module `forecastex/f1_wu.py`). Discovery (Feb-Jun
2026, 132-139 dates a test): the cities disagree — LA, Austin and Midway positive, **Miami significantly negative before 10:00 (−7.56¢,
t −2.85)** and Philadelphia negative, although every city has the same 55-68% gap; one carried, **UHLAX before 10:00: +5.00¢ a contract,
t 2.02**, 4 of 5 months positive, ~66,500 contracts a date (0.25 chance passes expected). **Sealed validation (2026-07-01 → 10-17, 109
dates): −1.48¢, t −0.47, placebo 33%, posterior −0.42¢ → REJECT.** Read: ForecastEx's temperature prices already account for its
Weather-Underground settlement; the per-city discovery means were noise around zero. Closed; no watchlist entry (net negative sealed).

## 728. F-family 2 protocol — ForecastEx hourly temperatures: the deciding METAR is public minutes before trading stops (S10)

**No trial spent. Written and committed BEFORE any trade is compared with any METAR or settlement.** Screen (§717): a **structural /
latency** edge. ForecastEx's hourly contracts ("will the temperature exceed X as of hh:00?", HRU*; listed since 2026-09-23) resolve on the
LAST Weather Underground observation in the hour ending hh:00, and trading runs until hh:00 (terms, `HRTermsandConditions.pdf`). Routine
METARs are at about :53, so the deciding reading is usually public ~5 minutes before the close. No-outcome timing screen (`pairs_hr`):
of 30,462 trades, 1,783 fall 3-7 minutes before the close, **551 of them at yes 10-90¢** (14,694 contracts in 26 days); 0-3 minutes:
76 of 1,003. Why might it be untaken? A thin retail venue and a minutes-long window that bots may not watch; against it, most post-:53
trades are already at extreme prices, so someone reacts. Data: IEM ASOS reports (routine + specials) for KLAX, KLGA, KSFO, KLAS, KMIA.
1. **Signal (fixed):** for each trade, the latest METAR with time in (hh:00 − 60 min, hh:00] and at least **3 minutes before the trade**
   (the publication-latency allowance); its temperature F = round(T-group °C × 9/5 + 32) (main-body °C if no T-group). **YES if F ≥ X + 2;
   NO if F ≤ X − 1;** otherwise no signal (the 1-2 °F margin absorbs WU's rounding).
2. **Trade:** where a trade printed the signalled side at ≤ 90¢, **buy that side at the printed price + 1¢ slippage + 1¢ fee**, hold to
   settlement. A later special report inside the hour can still flip the outcome; that risk is in the result.
3. **One pooled test** (5 cities). Statistic: each contract date's quantity-weighted mean net per contract; t over dates. Also reported:
   the signal's hit rate against settlement, and per city (descriptive).
4. **Discovery: contract dates 2026-09-23 → 10-07. Sealed: 10-08 → 10-18** (asserted in code). Carried if t > 1.96 and mean > 0 (the
   monthly condition is impossible in two weeks). Validation once as §664.4; watchlist per §133.
5. **Caveats fixed now:** METAR publication latency is assumed ≤ 3 min (to be measured live); fills at printed prices are an
   assumption to be checked live with IBKR quotes; trading needs the API's Read-Only flag off, which is the user's decision; capacity
   is bounded by the 10-90¢ trades in that window (~565 contracts a day across 5 cities).

## 729. F-family 2: the post-METAR window is already taken — not carried (S10)

**N 1,536 (no trial).** `reports/f2_discovery.json` (module `forecastex/f2_hourly.py`). Discovery (09-23 → 10-07): 47 signalled trades,
461 contracts, dated mean +14.8¢ but t 1.88 and **−$46.66 in total** (hit rate 62%: most signalled trades came before the :53 report, on an
earlier special). **Not carried; no validation.** Mapping check (settlements only, no prices): the contract hour is **Central time** and
the last METAR of that CT hour reproduces **100%** of 9,338 settlements (local-time reading 72-86%), so the implementation stands.
Descriptive, all 26 days: after the deciding report (+3 min) with a clear signal, the indicated side traded ≥ 97¢ in 103 trades (11,182
contracts), 91-96¢ in 53 (3,121), **≤ 90¢ in 9 (94 contracts)**; the 362 other post-report trades were within the rounding margin.
Someone reprices within minutes; the residue is ~$125 in 26 days across five cities. Closed.

## 730. Screen: ForecastEx release-timing errors (data public before trading stops) — none worth having (S10)

**No trial.** Mechanism: indicator contracts stop trading at a fixed Central-time "Resolution Time" while foreign agencies publish on
local clocks (e.g. SGCPI closes 00:00 CT; Singapore publishes 13:00 SGT = 23:00 CST in US winter), so a schedule slip would leave a
market open after the number is public. Screen over every Economic Indicators trade (`pairs_all/`, 810 days) and every settlement
(`prices_all/`): contracts whose winning side was ≤ 80¢ (median) 2-24 h before the close but printed ≥ 95¢ before it — **21 contracts in
9 products**, median 22-59 minutes early; trades of the winning side at ≤ 90¢ after that print: **21 trades, 210 contracts, $32.90**
(+1¢ slip and fee), all in USGP. ForecastEx's closes are set correctly and early information is repriced at once. Closed.

## 731. T-family 1 protocol — odd-lot tender offers: a measurement of a structural stream, not a fitted edge (S10)

**No trial spent. Written BEFORE any offer's profit is computed.** Screen (§717): **structural, small-capacity** — issuer tender offers
(SC TO-I) usually exempt holders of < 100 shares from proration, so 99 shares bought below the final tender price are all bought back at
it. Funds cannot scale 99 shares; the issuer, not competition, sets the price. EDGAR full-text search ("odd lot", SC TO-I, 2024-01 →
2026-10): 162 filings, 101 from listed issuers. The user's IBKR account can tender electronically.
1. **Rule (fixed):** for each listed issuer's original SC TO-I with odd-lot priority (offers that subject odd lots to proration excluded),
   **buy 99 shares at the close of the first trading day after the filing date**; tender all at the offer's final price (fixed price,
   Dutch-auction clearing price, or the NAV-based price, from the final SC TO-I/A); if terminated or not completed, sell at the close of
   the first trading day after the expiry. Costs: $2 a round trip. Exchange offers (paid in another company's shares) are listed apart.
2. **Reported:** per offer — type, buy price, final price, $ on 99 shares, days held; per year — offers, total $, capital needed at once.
   Not a statistical test: a positive total is a stream to forward-check on the next live offer, not a confirmation under §119.
3. **Caveats fixed now:** the close is an assumed fill (99 shares is far inside the volume of every listed name); prices from a free
   daily source; IBKR's corporate-action fee (if any) to be confirmed; one beneficial owner assumed.

## 732. T-family 1: odd-lot tenders are a real but small stream — about $2k a year, dominated by one exchange offer a year (S10)

**No trial (a measurement).** `reports/t1_oddlot.json` (module `tender/t1_oddlot.py`; EDGAR full text + submissions, Yahoo daily closes).
The automated parse is noisy (split-adjusted prices: COKE, MNST, RBNE; some odd-lot flags misread), so the totals below rest on the offers
checked by hand. **Disclosed rule flaw:** §731 buys even when the stock already trades above a fixed price (RUM, TORO, CFNB) — no one would;
an ex-ante filter (buy only below a fixed price or below a Dutch range's low end) is the obvious live rule, and is post hoc here.
- **Exchange offers (odd lots accepted in full every time; others prorated to 7-18%):** CMI→ATMU 2024 (12.030 ATMU a share) **+$4,791** on
  $26,314; LEN→MRP 2025 (4.137) **+$1,304** on $11,684; MDT→MMED 2026 (4.594) **−$915** on $9,281 — the subsidiary's price moves between the
  pricing window and the sale (MMED fell after expiry). Net ≈ +$5.2k in 2.8 years, ±10% risk on $9-26k each time.
- **Cash buybacks / fund tenders with odd-lot priority:** tens to low hundreds of dollars each (e.g. INCY +$290, SCHL +$111, JOF +$105,
  SWZ +$52, YEXT +$20 where the flags hold); many fund tenders subject odd lots to proration (BlackRock 2024, XFLT, NFJ); WEX −$370.
**Read:** the structural mechanism is genuine and cannot be competed away, but one beneficial owner earns roughly **$1.5-2.5k a year**,
lumpy and carried mostly by ~1 exchange offer a year with market risk (hedgeable by shorting the subsidiary in the pricing window).
Not an income stream at the scale sought; worth only a cheap EDGAR alert if the user wants one. No further work unless asked.

## 734. M-family protocol — live mention markets: the first-taker prize, the winners' latency, and a forward feed race (S10)

**No trial. Screen (§717 as loosened 2026-10-18: "why isn't everyone doing this?" — real-time transcription + a Kalshi bot + odd hours).**
Data: every public trade in YES-resolved KXTRUMPMENTION markets (`mention/m0_download.py`; trades before 2026-08-19 are under
`/historical/trades`). Kalshi does **not** halt a word's market when it is said (trading continues to the event's close).
1. **The prize (`m1_prize.py`, 3 most recent rallies, 36 words with a jump from ≤ 85¢):** takers buying YES at ≤ 90¢ in the jump to ≥ 95¢
   earned **$451 / $4,194 / $5,538 per event** net of the taker fee (mean ~$3.4k); the first taker instant took 36%; median 3 distinct
   taker instants a jump, median span 1.3 s. Example: "Massie" — one sweep at 19:34:32.475 bought ~5,000 YES at 43-95¢.
   **Full history (221 events with trades, 2025-04 → 2026-10; 2,079 jumps): $454,211 in total, mean $2,055 / median $1,073 an event,
   max $31,538; first instant 44%.** By month it grew with volume: 2025 $284-929 an event (first sweep 72-94%); 2026-02/03 peak $5.7-6.3k;
   2026-06 → 10 $1.4-2.5k an event, 16-19 events a month (~$24-47k a month across all fast takers; first sweep 41-56%).
2. **The winners' latency (`m2_latency.py`; RSBN live-stream recordings: actual start time + word-timed auto captions):** the first sweep
   comes **~7 s BEFORE the word on RSBN's recording timeline** — Wasilla 10-13 −7.6 s (n 5), Dalton 10-16 −6.9 s (n 13), Highland Heights
   10-17 −7.7 s (n 11, quartiles −7.8/−7.5). The tight spread says one mechanical pipeline on a feed faster than RSBN's; a live YouTube
   viewer of RSBN is later still, so **an RSBN-YouTube transcription bot would lose every race.**
3. **Forward test (fixed now):** for the 2026-10-19 Wichita rally (remarks ~23:00 UTC), `mention/m3_record.py` records the audio of 8
   public live streams (YouTube: RSBN, Forbes, LiveNOW from FOX, NTD, White House, C-SPAN, Fox News, ABC News) in 10-s chunks named by
   NTP-corrected UTC arrival time. Afterwards each sweep's ±40 s is transcribed offline (faster-whisper base.en, word timestamps) per
   stream. **Decision rule:** a public feed is viable only if, for ≥ 60% of jumps, the word arrives on it ≥ 1.5 s BEFORE the first sweep
   (the allowance for streaming ASR + order latency). If none is, the public-feed route is closed; a TV/satellite capture would be the
   remaining (hardware) route, for the user to decide.
4. **Other mention series (`mention/m4_series.py`; 458 series, settled since the 2026-08-19 cutoff, top 40 by volume):** nothing easier than
   the rallies — most are taken by ONE sweeper (first instant 70-98%, median 1-2 takers, median span < 1 s); per-event prize KXTRUMPSAY $2.2k,
   KXTRUMPMENTIONB $1.0k, KXFEDMENTION $2.6k (1 event), KXWORLDNEWSMENTION $392 (45 events), KXVANCEMENTION $610, KXMTPMENTION $555, most
   others $50-500. The whole arena (~$90-100k a month of first-taker prize) turns on the same question: can any feed we can get match the
   winners'? If public streams fail (step 3), the remaining candidate is over-the-air broadcast TV (USB tuner) on scheduled newscasts.
5. **Truth Social-triggered sweeps (`mention/m5_truth.py`; CNN's public archive of 36,968 posts with ms timestamps):** KXTRUMPSAY counts
   posts. 31 of 110 jumps follow a matching post ($10.1k of $21.9k); **sweep − post created_at: median 0.6 s, p10 0.2 s, p90 2.1 s** (monthly
   1.2 s, company 0.9 s). Truth Social returns 403 (Cloudflare) to plain requests from here. A sub-second incumbent for ~$6k a month: not
   worth the race. Closed.

## 736. R-family 1 protocol — Rotten Tomatoes score drift on Kalshi (KXRT): is YES on the upper strikes overpriced? (S10)

**No trial spent. Written BEFORE any KXRT price is compared with any outcome.** Screen (loosened §717): Kalshi's biggest data-publication
series (16.9M contracts in 23 movies since 2026-08-19; 58 more Jan-Aug 2026 under /historical). Each event: "Tomatometer above K on the
Monday after wide release at 10:00 ET", 10-19 strikes. The film-watcher folk rule: early (festival / embargo-day) reviews run kinder, so
scores drift down as the rest arrive. Hypothesis: Kalshi anchors on the current score, so YES on strikes near it is overpriced days before
settlement. Why isn't everyone doing it? A niche retail market; the drift is lore, not a posted number; it needs per-movie patience.
1. **Trade (fixed):** at the hourly candle ending 72 h and 48 h before the close, every strike whose yes mid ((bid + ask) / 2) is in
   [0.30, 0.70] with a live quote (bid > 0, ask < 1, spread ≤ 10¢): **buy NO at 1 − yes bid**, hold to settlement; Kalshi's taker fee
   ceil(7 × q × (1 − q)) ¢ at NO price q. **2 tests** (72 h, 48 h).
2. **Statistic:** each event's mean net per contract over its qualifying strikes; t over events. Also reported: the market-implied median
   (where the strikes' yes mids cross 0.5) minus the final score, per horizon.
3. **Discovery: events closing before 2026-06-01. Sealed: 2026-06-01 → 2026-10-19** (asserted in code). Carried: t > 1.96, mean > 0.
   Validation once as §664.4; watchlist per §133.
4. **Caveats fixed now:** candle quotes are the hour's last quote (fills assumed); strikes are correlated within an event (hence t over
   events, not strikes); capacity = the qualifying strikes' hourly volume.

hours with activity, so each horizon uses the last candle at or before it (within 6 h); /historical candles name prices `close`; older
markets store a label, so each event's final score is bracketed from its strike results. Discovery (closes before 2026-06-01): **72 h:
25 events, 30 strikes, +2.14¢ (t 0.23); 48 h: 13 events, 15 strikes, −18.81¢ (t −1.48)**; market-implied median − final **+0.41 pt
(t 0.79) / −0.34 pt (t −1.12)**, n 31. Not carried; no validation. Kalshi's RT markets already price the drift. Closed.

## 739. F-family 3 protocol — ForecastEx Nasdaq contracts (FNQ) in their last 15 minutes against the futures price (S10)

**No trial spent. Written BEFORE any FNQ trade is compared with any futures price or settlement.** Screen (loosened §717): an **access**
edge — ForecastEx is reachable only through IBKR, and its FNQ contracts ("will lead-month Nasdaq-100 futures settle above K?", ~16,000
a day, trading to 15:00 CT, settled on CME's daily settlement) are quoted by retained market makers for IBKR retail. In the last minutes
the outcome is nearly fixed by where the futures trade. Why isn't everyone doing it? It needs both an IBKR ForecastEx account and a
futures feed; the window is minutes a day. Against it: retained MMs hedge with futures and may already price it.
1. **Signal (fixed):** each FNQ trade (pair) between 14:45 and 15:00 CT on its contract date; the lead-month MNQ 1-minute close for the
   last minute ending at least 1 minute before the trade (latency allowance); distance d = (F − K) / F. **YES if d ≥ +0.25%, NO if
   d ≤ −0.25%**, else no signal.
2. **Trade:** where the signalled side printed at ≤ 90¢, buy it at the printed price + 1¢ slippage + 1¢ fee; hold to settlement.
3. **One test.** Statistic: each contract date's quantity-weighted mean net per contract; t over dates; signal hit rate reported.
4. **Discovery: contract dates before 2026-03-01. Sealed: 2026-03-01 → 2026-10-09** (the end of the futures data; asserted in code).
   Carried if t > 1.96 and mean > 0; validation once as §664.4; watchlist per §133. Capacity: qualifying contracts a day.

## 742. C-family 1 — Kalshi combos (RFQ parlays): the sellers' margin, and a protocol to price them from their legs (S10)

**No trial. Screen (loosened §717): structural + access.** Combos (MVE) are created on request (RFQ); makers answer with a yes bid and
a no bid for the full size, the requester takes the best; quotes are private; any member may quote via the API per Kalshi (Sportico),
onboarding unverified; Oddpool (2026-05, 270 test RFQs) saw ~5 combo-only makers, 2.7-3.7 quoting each request, responses < 300 ms,
**inside combo spread 40.5¢**. Why isn't everyone doing it? It needs a multi-leg pricing engine, a live WebSocket/REST quoting bot and
capital, against a few incumbents. **Calibration (`combo/c1_calib.py`; 149,754 settled combos, 204M contracts, the latest ~30k in each
of five MVE series):** sellers kept **$1.97M on $11.44M of premium (17%)**; by price band the seller earned 1.6¢ (2-5¢ band), 3.4¢
(5-10¢), **5.9¢ (10-20¢), 7.5¢ (20-35¢)** a contract; 35-65¢ about fair; 65-95¢ the buyer +4-5¢ (sellers underprice favourites).
**C-family 1 protocol (fixed now, before any leg price is looked up):** a stratified sample of settled combos in
KXMVESPORTSMULTIGAMEEXTENDED and KXMVECROSSCATEGORY whose legs are all in **different events** (no two legs share an event_ticker:
treated as independent). Fair value = the product over legs of each leg's own Kalshi mid (side-adjusted) at the last 1-minute candle
before the combo opened. Report (a) executed price ÷ fair (the incumbents' markup) by price band, (b) calibration of FAIR against
results (is the product unbiased?), (c) the P&L of a seller who quotes YES at max(fair × 1.15, fair + 1¢) and wins every combo where
that undercuts the executed price — net of Kalshi's fee. Descriptive (no trial); a positive (c) with (b) unbiased means a forward
shadow test on live RFQs (no orders) is next, which needs the user's Kalshi API key (on the droplet) — the user's call.

## 743. C-family 1 result: the leg-product cannot price combos historically; the sellers' margin is real but band-specific (S10)

**No trial.** `combo/c2_legs.py`, `reports/c2_legs.json` (1,336 of 1,500 sampled combos priced). First pass took empty books (bid 0 /
ask 1 → a fake 50¢ mid) and stale candles — fixed to a real two-sided quote (spread ≤ 10¢) ≤ 5 min old; the result is still unusable:
by band the leg product misses the outcome by 4-46 points (65-95¢: product 0.50 vs YES rate 0.96). Two reasons, seen by hand: (1)
crypto 15-minute legs in one window (BTC/ETH/HYPE/… "down") are one bet, not independent — six legs at ~75% multiply to 17% while the
combo trades at 81% and wins; (2) many combos are built in play, when legs are nearly decided. Takers (150 sampled combos): **85% of
contracts are YES buys** — so §742's calibration is the parlay buyers' result: they **overpay on 2-35¢ combos (sellers +1.6 to +7.5¢)
and are underpriced on 65-95¢ in-play combos (buyers +4-5¢)**. Quoting at fair × 1.15 on the (wrong) product loses $34k — a statement
about the product, not about quoting. A quoter needs a correlation-aware, live pricing engine; only a live shadow test (RFQs on the
authenticated WebSocket, our would-be quote vs the executed price vs settlement, no orders) can measure it. Pending the user's decision
on API access.

## 744. C-family 1 forward shadow test deployed on the droplet (user-approved 2026-10-19; read-only, no orders) (S10)

**No trial.** `kalshi_lip/rfq_shadow.py` runs as systemd `kalshi-rfq-shadow` in /opt/kalshi-lip (venv + `websockets` added), with the
user's existing Kalshi key (only KALSHI_KEY_ID / KALSHI_KEY_PATH exported; the key is never read by us). It subscribes to the
authenticated `communications` channel and NEVER creates RFQs or quotes. **Observed: > 1,000 RFQs a second** (73,282 created and 71,778
deleted in one minute; most $10 target-cost requests withdrawn within the minute) — so it logs a deterministic 0.1% hash-sample of RFQ
ids (~36 a minute, ~300 MB a day): the RFQ (legs, size, created_ts), each leg's top of book at that moment (batch orderbooks, ≤ 4 req/s),
and the RFQ's deletion; it stops writing below 10 GB free disk. Analysis (to write once data accrues): join each sampled RFQ's combo
ticker to its public trades (executed price, taker side) and settlement; price it from the leg books (crypto legs in one window
grouped as one bet; in-play combos flagged); measure a would-be quoter's wins and P&L after fees, by price band.
**Parked (user, 2026-10-19):** new strategies must start on ~$100-200. Combo quoting is capital-bound (a 15¢ parlay ties up 85¢ until
settlement): $200 sells ~$35 of premium a cycle, ~$3-7 at a 10-20% edge — a test, not income. The sample's seller margin is also noisy
by window (KXMVESPORTSMULTIGAMEEXTENDED Aug 17-30: 0.4% of premium; cross-category windows 38-71%). The read-only shadow logger keeps
running ~2 days so the evidence exists for later; then it is stopped. Revisit once another stream funds the capital.

## 747. M-family 2 protocol — in-speech decay: is YES on still-unsaid words overpriced mid-speech? (S10)

**No trial. Written BEFORE any unsaid-word price is compared with any result.** Screen (§717 loosened; user's scale + $100-200 rules):
not a speed race — a hazard question. While Trump speaks, an unsaid word's YES should fall as time runs out; retail holding YES "in
hope" would leave NO cheap. Capacity: ~20 unsaid words an event at thousands of contracts each, ~16-19 events a month; capital recycles
nightly. Why isn't everyone doing it? It needs per-word hazard judgement while live; mention traders are fans of a word, not of NO.
Data: every public trade of KXTRUMPMENTION markets — said words (`mention_trades/<event>.json`) and unsaid words (`<event>.no.json`,
`mention/m0_download.py --no`).
1. **Clock:** speech start = the event's first jump (m1: the first taker sweep of a said word) — what a live bot sees.
2. **Rule (fixed):** at τ ∈ {15, 30, 45} min after the start, every market of the event that has not yet jumped (no trade ≥ 90¢ so far)
   and whose last YES print is in [0.10, 0.60]: **buy NO at 1 − last YES print + 1¢ slippage**, Kalshi taker fee, hold to settlement.
   **3 tests.** Statistic: each event's mean net per contract; t over events; also the hit rate and the next-10-min volume (capacity).
3. **Discovery: events closing before 2026-06-01; sealed: 2026-06-01 → 2026-10-19.** Carried t > 1.96, mean > 0; validation once per
   §664.4; watchlist per §133.
4. **Caveats fixed now:** the last print is not the NO ask (1¢ slippage is the allowance); "start" can lag the true start (it errs late,
   which is conservative for a decay trade); words said during the speech jump and are excluded only from τ on.
**Withdrawn before any test (user, 2026-10-19):** its capacity estimate (~$50-300 an event, ~$1-5k a month, depth-capped) is below the
user's scale bar, so it is not worth the download. No trial spent; the module stays unrun. Rule going forward: the capacity screen
comes BEFORE any download.

none. §742's 17% historical margin sits in long-shot / in-play / correlated combos, where the incumbents' models beat a leg product.
**Closed.** `kalshi-rfq-shadow` stopped and disabled on the droplet (data kept: /opt/kalshi-lip/rfq).

## 756. K-family 10 protocol — favourite/long-shot bias in Kalshi game-winner markets (autonomous session, 2026-10-20) (S10)

**No trial spent. Written BEFORE any game-winner price is compared with any result.** Screen (user rules): legitimate venue (Kalshi);
small start; capacity is the deepest on the exchange (millions of contracts a game); no keys needed to test (keys only to trade —
tabled until the user is back). K-family 1 found no long-shot bias in index brackets (§665), but sports books are known for it and
Kalshi sports are retail-heavy. Why isn't everyone doing it? If it exists, it would be eaten by makers — this is a check that the
market is calibrated, cheap to run on public data.
1. **Data:** settled KXNFLGAME, KXNBAGAME, KXMLBGAME, KXNHLGAME (+ KXNCAAFGAME, KXNCAABGAME where present) via `kalshi/download.py`
   (live + /historical, hourly candles).
2. **Price (fixed):** the hourly candle ending 6 h before the market's close (pre-game for every sport; games end ≤ ~4 h after
   start), quote filter bid > 0, ask < 1, spread ≤ 5¢; one market per game (the team listed first in the event's markets, to avoid
   counting both sides of one game).
3. **Trades (fixed), Kalshi taker fee ceil(7·q(1−q))¢ at price q:** (a) long-shot side: YES mid ≤ 25¢ → **buy NO at 1 − YES bid**;
   (b) favourite side: YES mid ≥ 75¢ → **buy YES at the ask**. **2 tests per sport, pooled across sports = 2 tests** (sport-level shown,
   not tested). Statistic: per-game net per contract; t over games; monthly sign shown.
4. **Discovery: games closing before 2025-10-01. Sealed: 2025-10-01 → 2026-10-19.** Carried t > 1.96, mean > 0; validation once per
   §664.4; watchlist per §133. Capacity reported (volume at the 6 h candle).

## 757. F-family 5 protocol — favourite/long-shot bias across every ForecastEx product (autonomous session) (S10)

**No trial. Written BEFORE any ForecastEx price is compared with any settlement in this family** (families 1-4 used only UH*/HRU*/FNQ
late windows). Data on disk: every trade (`forecastex/pairs_all`, 810 days) and every settlement (`prices_all`). ForecastEx is IBKR's
retail venue — where a long-shot bias is most plausible. Trading would need the user's IBKR/TWS session → tabled if it passes.
1. **Trades (fixed):** every pair priced at least 24 h before its contract's expiration: (a) yes ≤ 15¢ → **buy NO at the pair's NO
   price + 1¢**; (b) yes ≥ 85¢ → **buy YES at the pair's YES price + 1¢**; 1¢ ForecastEx fee; hold to settlement. **2 tests.**
2. **Statistic:** each contract-expiry event's (product + expiration date) quantity-weighted mean net per contract; t over events;
   product categories shown, not tested.
3. **Discovery: expirations before 2026-03-01; sealed 2026-03-01 → 2026-10-19.** Carried t > 1.96, mean > 0; validation per §664.4.

+ game), 332 filled. **Sports same-game YES fills 226: executed ÷ independent product median 1.23 (makers add for correlation); settled
208: YES 1.0% vs executed 2.1% vs independent 1.4%; buyers −$12,546 on $12,576.** Crypto same-window: ×2.56, buyers −$669 on $1,032.
No requester edge. Closed.
