## 766. CORRECTION to §763-765: with their real consistency rules, TradeDay and LucidPro are NEGATIVE at zero edge — only Tradeify stands (S10)

**No trial.** Two rules left out of the earlier models reverse the result. **TradeDay 2.0** (relaunched 2026-05; reviews 2026-06/07):
Quick Pay has a **5-day minimum and a 30% evaluation consistency cap**; with them (fee $87 with code): **−$2,861 (50% split) / −$2,475
(80%) a run.** **LucidPro**: funded payouts need the best day ≤ **40% of the cycle's profit** (modelled with the "cycle" scheme:
cycle_days 1, cons_f 0.40, buffer $2,100, min $500, max $2,000): **−$5,236 / −$3,376** (was +$9-11k without it). The bracket game's
+$1,200 winning days rarely sit below 40% (or 30%) of the needed profit, so consistency rules destroy the option value. **So §764's
TradeDay and §763-765's LucidPro figures, and §765's three-firm / two-firm portfolios, are WITHDRAWN.** The zero-edge survey now reads:
**positive — Tradeify Select Daily only (+$5.5k a run; its rules confirmed with the user); negative or unproven — every other firm
modelled.** Lesson: consistency and payout-gating rules dominate a firm's structural value; only a firm with verified rules counts.
(Elite Trader Funding's promo-price result also omits its "active trade days" rule — treat as negative.)
Smaller size at LucidPro (to fit the 40% rule): sim size ×0.3 / ×0.5 / ×0.7 → **−$1,130 / −$2,062 / −$3,149** a run — still negative
(small size rarely reaches the $3,000 target before fees pile up). Lucid closed.
LucidFlex (no funded consistency; 50% evaluation consistency; 5 winning days ≥ $150; ≤ 50% of profit and ≤ $2,000 a payout): **−$1,409
($130) / −$3,589 ($175).** Firm thread closed: **Tradeify Select Daily is the only modelled firm whose structure pays with no edge** —
worth knowing when choosing a second firm later (an edge would be required elsewhere).
Tradeify mixes at zero edge ($116): **NKD×5 +$5,929 / +$3,797; 3 NKD + 2 FDXM (the plan) +$5,523 / +$3,783; 2 NKD + 3 FDXM +$5,213 /
+$3,692; the demo's five-product mix +$2,524 / +$1,574.** The planned mix is near the zero-edge best and adds FDXM's independent signal
— no change needed whether or not the edges hold.

`bestAskQuote`, no key); Kalshi lists the same lines (KXNBAPTS/REB/AST/3PT, "Name: N+"). Props books are thinner, so gaps may be wider.
- **Match:** same game, player full name, stat, threshold ("at least N" ↔ "N+").
- **Net of fees, both legs taker:** buy YES on one venue at its ask and NO on the other (1 − its YES bid); net = 1 − cost − Kalshi
  0.07·p(1−p) − Polymarket feeCoefficient·p(1−p). Size = the smaller top-of-book quantity (books fetched only for net > 0).
- **Sweep** every 5 minutes, NBA games starting within 12 h, ~6 hours. **Pass (fixed now):** ≥ 5 distinct positive-net pairs a day
  with a median top size ≥ $50 and median net ≥ 1¢ → worth an account conversation (both venues need the user's KYC; Polymarket US
  allowed in TX per §714). Otherwise closed.

## 774. K-family 13 registered: favourite / underdog mispricing in Kalshi ESPORTS match winners, before the scheduled start (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any esports price or outcome is looked at.** Why esports: year-round (daily
matches across titles), large and growing volume (outcome-free screen, settled contracts: LoL match winner ≈ 10.5 M Aug / 50 M Sep /
26 M Oct-to-date; CS2 map ≈ 8 M Oct; Dota 2 ≈ 8 M a month; R6 ≈ 2.5 M Sep; Valorant total maps ≈ 0.3-0.4 M), and plausibly fewer
professional market makers anchoring prices than the major leagues (K10, §756, found the majors fair). Esports markets close at the
match's END, so the entry is anchored to the scheduled start in the event ticker (`lean.py --start`).
- **Universe (fixed):** KXLOLGAME, KXCS2GAME, KXDOTA2GAME, KXVALORANTGAME, KXR6GAME, KXRLGAME, KXOWGAME, KXCODGAME, KXMLBBGAME.
- **Entry (amended in §775: 4 h → 1 h before):** last hourly candle ending in the 3 h before the scheduled start; spread ≤ 5¢; one market an event — the side with the
  higher mid. **favourite_YES:** its mid ≥ 0.70 → buy YES at its ask. **underdog_YES:** the other side's mid ≤ 0.30 → buy that side's
  YES at its ask. Taker fee ceil(7·p(1−p))¢. Unit: the event (one bet each); t over events.
- **Discovery:** matches starting before 2026-08-20, 300 random events a series (`--sample 300`, seeded by series). A test is carried
  only with discovery t > 1.96 and mean > 0; at most one direction can be.
- **Sealed:** matches starting 2026-08-20 → 2026-10-19, every event; ONE look at the carried test with the §664.4 rule (seed 774),
  §133 watchlist otherwise. Capacity reported as contracts traded in the entry candle and over the market's life.

## 775. K-family 13 amended BEFORE any outcome: Kalshi's esports start times can be wrong by hours (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539.** Checked against Riot's public schedule (esports-api.lolesports.com) while screening in-play capacity:
KXLOLGAME-26OCT151900KCC9 says "scheduled Oct 15 7:00 PM EDT" (23:00Z) but KC-C9 started 18:00Z and the market CLOSED 22:49Z, before
its own listed start (Kalshi swapped KC-C9 and MVK-FUR). With §774's window (3 h → 0 h before the listed start) such matches would be
entered in play. **Amended:** the entry candle is the last one ending in the window **4 h → 1 h before the listed start** (a 1 h
buffer against small errors), and an event is **dropped if its market closed < 20 min after the listed start** (impossible as
scheduled). Everything else in §774 unchanged. The partial download (0 rows written) was discarded and restarted with this window.

## 776. A94 protocol: LoL in-play — does Riot's public livestats feed beat Kalshi's sweep? (live, no money) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any live data is recorded.** Outcome-free capacity screen (12 recent DCGI/Worlds matches on
KXLOLGAME): fast moves (≥ 15¢ within 60 s) leave value swept at stale prices of median $427, mean $1.3k, max $5.3k a match (trades
in the move's direction within 20 s, valued at the 1-5 min later median). Kalshi's LoL match markets trade 10-50 M contracts a month;
LoL runs ~10 months a year (Worlds → off-season Nov-Jan); CS2/Dota/Valorant lack a comparable free live feed (HLTV is Cloudflare-
gated, Dota spectating is delayed 2+ min). Historical frames: the one usable alignment so far (MVK-FUR, 2026-10-15) shows an
inhibitor in Riot's frames at 23:46:09.2Z and Kalshi's first move trade at 23:46:15.1Z (+6.0 s) — but frame timestamps are game-server
times, not publication times, so only a live recording answers the question.
- **Recorder:** `esports/a94_lolrace.py` (Riot frames with first-received time, every 1 s; Kalshi trades on the live match, every
  1 s; NTP offset). Runs: EMEA Masters 2026-10-22 12:00Z; Worlds 2026-10-23 17:00Z → ~03:00Z (8 matches).
- **Jump:** a Kalshi move ≥ 15¢ within 60 s; its first trade ≥ 5¢ from the pre-move price = the sweep time. The game event = the last
  Riot state change (kills, towers, inhibitors, barons, dragons, game end) before the sweep. **Lead = sweep time − our receive time
  of that frame** (NTP-corrected).
- **Pass (fixed now):** lead ≥ 1.5 s on ≥ 60% of ≥ 10 jumps, AND the value still available after receive + 1.0 s (stale-price trades
  after that time, valued as above) has a median ≥ $300 a match. Otherwise closed. A pass is still only a measurement: trading needs
  the user's Kalshi API key (tabled until they are back), and a §119-style forward test.

## 777. K-family 14 registered: in-play under-reaction in Kalshi VALORANT match markets — follow a fast move, no game feed (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any rule P&L is computed.** Screen (outcome-free price paths, 15-19 recent
matches a title with > 50k contracts): buying in a fast move's direction X s after its first trade, valued at the 60-120 s later
median, net of fee and counting losers: **Valorant +$449 / +$393 / +$334 / +$133 a match at 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 s; LoL +$234 / +$114 /
+$47 / +$43; CS2 −$34 / −$48 / −$61 / −$55.** (A first version counting only positive trades overstated all three — corrected.) If
Valorant prices under-react for 10+ s, a bot needs no game data: Kalshi's own trades are the signal. Valorant was picked from that
screen, so the sealed test is FORWARD only.
- **Data:** every KXVALORANTGAME event's trades (one market an event; `kalshi/k14_valmom.py download`).
- **Signal (causal):** a trade whose price is ≥ 10¢ from the median of the market's trades 120 s → 10 s before it (≥ 3 trades
  there); no other signal in the previous 120 s. Direction = the move's.
- **Entry:** the first trade ≥ 5 s after the signal whose taker side is the move's direction, at its price + taker fee (a taker
  arriving 5 s late). **Exit:** VWAP of the market's trades 60-120 s after the signal, minus 1¢ (half a spread) and the taker fee.
  Unit: the signal; per-match mean P&L, t over matches.
- **Discovery:** every match settled before 2026-10-20 20:00Z (including the 16 screened). Carried with discovery t > 1.96, mean > 0,
  AND positive in ≥ 2 of the 3 calendar-quarter blocks the data spans.
- **Sealed = forward:** matches starting after 2026-10-20 20:00Z, evaluated once at ≥ 60 matches with signals (or 2026-12-31,
  whichever first); §664.4 rule (seed 777); §133 otherwise. Trading itself needs the user's Kalshi API key (tabled until they are back).

## 779. A95 protocol: Kalshi BTC 15-minute markets in their averaging minute — does the book lag the partly-known average? (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any price is recorded.** KXBTC15M (≈ 3 M contracts ≈ $1.5 M a market, every 15 minutes, all
year) resolves on the simple average of the 60 one-second BRTI prints before the close, against the same average before the open
(`floor_strike`); trading runs to the close. In the last minute part of the average is already fixed and the rest is narrow, so the
fair price is computable from public exchange data. Surely bot-contested; the question is whether a residue above fees is left.
- **Recorder** (`kalshi/a95_btc15.py`): every second from 120 s before each close to the close: Coinbase BTC-USD ticker (public REST,
  BRTI proxy), Kalshi's current KXBTC15M order book top (bid/ask/size), receive times. ~3 hours (12 markets) to start.
- **Fair value:** known part = mean of the recorded proxy prints already inside the window; remaining k seconds: proxy now plus a
  Brownian average with σ from the last 15 min of 1 s returns; P(YES) = Φ((mean_known·(60−k)/60 + S·k/60 − strike) / (σ_S·√(k³/3)/60)).
  Proxy basis vs BRTI (Coinbase ≠ BRTI by a few dollars) is estimated per market from the open-average vs floor_strike and removed.
- **Pass (fixed now):** median over markets of the best executable edge (fair − ask − fee, or bid − fair − fee) ≥ 2¢ on ≥ $100 of top
  size in the last 60 s, in ≥ 50% of markets. Otherwise closed (bots already price it). Trading would need the user's API key.

## 781. A95: Kalshi's BTC 15-minute books price the averaging minute — a public single-exchange proxy cannot beat them; closed (S10)

**No trial.** Historical supplement `kalshi/a95h_btc15_hist.py` (30 recent markets with ≥ $1k of last-minute risk; Coinbase trades
rebuilt to 1 s as the BRTI proxy): **last-minute takers' net median −$1,093 a market; median taker edge −0.1¢ to −0.7¢ in almost
every market**. The proxy settles $0.6-13.8 away from Kalshi's expiration_value (median |err| $4.1) — in a close contest's last
seconds that error is larger than any edge, and the few big positive totals (+$80.8k, +$56.7k, +$21.9k) are exactly the markets
with $4-7 proxy errors, i.e. the model's error, not the book's. Last-minute capacity is real ($50-180k of risk in close
contests) but the book tracks BRTI; an edge would need a live BRTI replica from every constituent exchange's order book — what the
crypto firms in these markets already run. The live recorder (§779) caught one market before a container restart; not resumed.
Closed. Also: the laptop container restarted a third time — the futres-* services came back on their own.

## 782. A96 protocol: ProphetX offers vs Pinnacle — forward paper bets scored on closing-line value (no money) (S10)

**No trial at registration (one when evaluated); N 1,539. Written BEFORE any paper bet is recorded.** ProphetX (CFTC DCM since
2026-06; peer-to-peer exchange; reviews: 48 states, not MN/NV → Texas served, to confirm in-app; fee 2% of net winnings, 1% on
NBA/NCAAB per one source — 2% used throughout) publishes its order book on a keyless public API (`/trade/public/api/v1/events`,
`/v2/events/{id}/markets`: best back odds per side with the stake behind them). One outcome-free snapshot (2026-10-20 ~23:00Z,
185 two-way moneyline sides matched to Pinnacle's guest API): **19 sides EV > 0 after the 2%, 7 > +2%, $7.3k of stake at EV > 0**;
mostly NFL favourites days before kick-off (DAL −166 vs no-vig 65.3% → +3.8% on $228; HOU −315 +3.6%; LAR −172 +3.2%).
- **Recorder** (`sports/a96_prophetx.py`, service futres-a96): every 10 min, ProphetX events starting within 7 days (tennis, NFL/NCAAF,
  NHL, NBA, MMA, esports, MLB) × Pinnacle pre-match moneylines; both logged.
- **Paper bet:** a side whose best ProphetX back price has EV ≥ +2% vs Pinnacle's proportional no-vig after the 2% fee, with ≥ $25
  behind it; size = min(available, $100); at most one paper bet per side per 6 h.
- **Score:** closing-line EV = p_close·(D−1)·0.98 − (1 − p_close), p_close = Pinnacle no-vig in the last snapshot before the start.
  Outcomes recorded too (secondary; too noisy to decide at this size).
- **Pass (fixed now):** ≥ 150 paper bets; mean closing-line EV ≥ +1.0% with t > 1.645 (per bet) and > 0 in ≥ 3 of 4 sport groups
  present; AND capacity: the expected value of the week's qualifying stake (Σ size × closing EV) ≥ $500 a week → toward the user's
  $2k/month bar. Otherwise closed. Betting is manual-capable (days-ahead NFL), so no API key is needed to act.

## 786. Screen: ProphetX's flow is large; quoting it needs its market-maker programme — tabled for the user (S10)

**No trial.** A96's recorder now logs each market's matched stake. Between two sweeps (00:35Z → 00:54Z, a Tuesday evening):
**$526k matched — NFL spreads $298k, NFL totals $71k, NBA spreads/totals $85k, NFL moneylines $32k** (≈ $1.5 M an hour even if
the figure counts both sides). Taking stale offers is small (A96: ~$1k a sweep at EV ≥ 2%); quoting against that flow is not.
But: (1) the public websocket channels carry only best-line / liquidity / score changes — matched wagers are private, so the flow's
adverse selection (soft vs sharp) cannot be measured from outside; (2) ProphetX's official fee page (v1.3, 2026-10-12) charges 2%
of net gains on straight trades; its market-maker page offers onboarding (zero-fee high-frequency API per its marketing) by contact
only. A 2%-fee user quoting at the best price cannot be +EV against zero-fee professional quoters (the books already sit ~0-2%
from Pinnacle before fees). **Tabled until the user is back:** an approach to ProphetX's market-maker programme (terms, capital,
API) is the only route; then a shadow quote test with their private fill feed. A96 (taking) keeps recording.

## 787. A97 protocol: ProphetX positive-EV offer episodes in real time — capacity and competition for A96 (no money) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any episode is recorded.** ProphetX's public Pusher websocket (`ws.prophetx.co`, key from its
public `/pusher/public/connection-config`; channel `public-broadcast-service=1-device_type=1-event={id}`) pushes every liquidity change
with the line's full current ladder (6 NBA games: 1,433 updates a minute). A96's 20-minute snapshots only see offers that survived;
A97 measures how much positive-EV stake appears and how fast it is taken.
- **Recorder** (`sports/a97_pxstream.py`, service futres-a97): subscribes to NFL / NCAAF / NBA / NHL events starting within 3 days
  (refreshed hourly); full-game moneyline / spread / total market ids from one REST call per event (props share the "total" type);
  Pinnacle no-vig refreshed every 2 min (same matching and lines as A96, §783). An **episode** = the best back offer on a side has EV ≥
  +2% after the 2% fee; logged: start, end, odds, stake behind it at start and its minimum, end reason (EV < 2% because the offer was
  taken / pulled / Pinnacle moved).
- **Readout** (after ≥ 3 days incl. a weekend): +EV stake appearing per day by sport; median episode lifetime; share of episodes
  ending in < 10 s (contested). Feeds A96's ≥ $500-a-week capacity criterion — a lifetime of seconds means a bot race, hours means
  manual-capable. Outcome-free; no trial.

## 788. CORRECTION to §786: ProphetX's "totalStake" is RESTING liquidity, not matched volume — the $526k figure is not flow (S10)

**No trial.** Checked over 8 minutes on 4 NFL events: the REST `totalStake` of a market fell by $36,000 while the websocket's summed
`traded_value` for it was −$36,033 (moneyline −$4,476 vs −$6,027+1,551; total −$5,401 vs −$4,564+64). `totalStake` is the stake
resting on the book and `traded_value` its change (posts and pulls); neither is matched volume. §786's "$526k matched in 20 minutes"
counted only increases in resting stake — liquidity being posted, not trades. **ProphetX's traded volume is not public**; the
maker-route capacity is unknown, and the adverse-selection question remains unanswerable from outside. §786's tabling stands
(it needs the user and ProphetX's market-maker programme); the "large flow" premise is withdrawn. Also: market ids are per
market TYPE (shared across events) — A96 keys by (event, market), so its records are unaffected.

## 792. A96 caveat (no rule change): its tennis "edges" are a proportional-devig artifact on extreme long shots (S10)

**No trial; the §782 pass rule is unchanged and will be applied as registered — this entry is how to read it.** Almost every tennis
side A96 flags at EV ≥ +2% is a long shot at +600…+4,300 (e.g. +4,000 at 2.4% implied vs Pinnacle 3.15% proportional no-vig).
Proportional devig spreads Pinnacle's margin evenly, which over-states long shots — most where margins are widest (lower-tier
tennis, ITF median −12%). A power-devig sensitivity (raw Pinnacle prices logged since ~06:00Z 2026-10-21, `a96_prophetx.power`):
on the first 6 closed paper bets **closing-line EV +13.3% proportional vs −19.2% power**. Unless that sign survives at n ≥ 150, a
proportional "pass" would be the method's bias, not an edge — the morning brief and the final A96 verdict report both. A97's
"pinnacle_moved" endings are mostly Pinnacle shifting its main line (the old line's fair disappears), not Pinnacle moving to
ProphetX's price; start/end fair prices are now logged to separate the two.

**No trial.** §783 enters spread/total bets only at Pinnacle's main line, but scored them only if that same line was still Pinnacle's

every Pinnacle full-game spread/total line (main and alternate, proportional no-vig) for the matched events (`lines_*.jsonl`), and a
spread/total bet is scored at its own line from the last Pinnacle snapshot before the start. Moneylines unchanged. No spread/total
paper bet had closed when this was written (2026-10-21 ~12:40Z).

## 794. A98 protocol: steam lag — does Kalshi's game-line book lag Pinnacle's moves? (live, no money) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any price is recorded.** Every book checked sits on Pinnacle's price (§785, §790); the open
question is TIMING. When Pinnacle moves a moneyline (news, sharp money), Kalshi's market makers must follow; if they lag, Kalshi's
stale side can be taken. Kalshi game books are deep (tens of millions of contracts a game), so a real lag has capacity.
- **Recorder** (`sports/a98_steam.py`, ≈ 20 s cadence): Pinnacle guest-API moneylines (proportional no-vig; near-even prices dominate)
  for NBA / NHL / NFL / NCAAF games starting within 24 h; Kalshi top of book (yes bid/ask) for the matched KXNBAGAME / KXNHLGAME /
  KXNFLGAME / KXNCAAFGAME markets (one public listing call per series). Both logged with receive times.
- **Move:** Pinnacle no-vig changes ≥ 2 percentage points between consecutive polls. **Opportunity at +20 / +40 / +60 / +120 s:**
  new fair − Kalshi ask − fee (up-moves) or Kalshi bid − new fair − fee (down-moves).
- **Pass (fixed now):** over ≥ 3 days with ≥ 20 moves: median opportunity at +20 s ≥ +1¢ AND ≥ 1¢ on ≥ 50% of moves. Otherwise closed
  (Kalshi follows Pinnacle within one poll). Trading would need the user's Kalshi API key.

## 795. K-family 15 registered: favourite / long-shot bias in Kalshi's NON-sports, non-index markets (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any price is joined to any outcome.** K1 (§665) covered only S&P/Nasdaq brackets
and K10 (§756) sports — both sit on a sharp anchor. The literature reports the bias elsewhere: Kalshi contracts < 20¢ under-perform and
> 80¢ out-perform their prices (Becker, trade-level); political markets compressed toward 50% (arXiv 2602.19520). Non-sports markets have
no Pinnacle-style anchor, so a bias could survive there.
- **Universe:** settled markets closing 2026-06-01 → 2026-10-20, event category in {Politics, Elections, Economics, Climate and Weather,
  World, Entertainment, Science and Technology, Companies, Health, Social, Culture} (not Sports, Financials, Crypto, Exotics), market
  volume ≥ 1,000 contracts (`kalshi/k15_nonsports.py`).
- **Entry:** last hourly candle ending 27 h → 24 h before the close; spread ≤ 5¢. **favourite_YES:** mid ≥ 0.80 → buy YES at the ask;
  **longshot_NO:** mid ≤ 0.20 → buy NO at 1 − bid; taker fee. Unit: the event (mean over its qualifying markets); t over events.
- **Discovery:** closes 2026-06-01 → 2026-08-31 (≤ 4,000 markets sampled by event, seeded). Carried: t > 1.96, mean > 0 and > 0 in ≥ 2
  categories. **Sealed:** 2026-09-01 → 2026-10-20, once, carried tests only; §664.4 rule (seed 795); §133 otherwise.
- **Capacity:** volume in the entry candle and the market's life, per category, reported before any sealed look.

## 796. K-family 16 registered: sell long shots as a MAKER in Kalshi's non-sports markets (zero maker fee) — trade-level markout (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any trade is joined to an outcome.** Becker's Kalshi trade study (gross of fees): makers
+1.12% a contract overall, but Media +3.64%, World Events +3.66%, Entertainment +2.40%, Weather +1.29% (Sports +1.12%, Finance +0.08%);
the gap is driven by takers buying cheap YES (at 1¢ takers −57%, makers +57%). Kalshi's fee check (2026-10-21): almost every non-sports
series is fee type `quadratic` — **takers only; makers pay nothing** (2,589 of 2,596 Entertainment, all 143 World, 458 Climate, 2,257 of
2,264 Politics). So a resting offer that sells cheap YES (= buys NO) in these categories keeps the whole markout. Our own NFL markout
(§790) was negative — sports flow is informed; the question is whether non-sports flow is not.
- **Data:** public trades of the K15 universe (§795) markets (same sample), `kalshi/k16_makerls.py`.
- **Fill = every trade where the TAKER bought YES at ≤ 20¢** (a resting YES-sell / NO-buy filled at that price). Maker P&L a contract =
  price − (1 if YES else 0); no fee. Also reported: 20-35¢, and by time to close (> 7 d, 1-7 d, 6-24 h, < 6 h — late fills are where
  news sweeps resting quotes).
- **Unit:** the event (contract-weighted mean of its fills); t over events. **Discovery:** closes 2026-06-01 → 08-31; carried with
  t > 1.96, mean > 0, > 0 in ≥ 2 categories. **Sealed:** 2026-09-01 → 10-20, once (seed 796); §664.4; §133 otherwise.
- **Capacity:** contracts traded at ≤ 20¢ by takers buying YES, per category per week — the pool a quoter could share. Acting needs the
  user's Kalshi API key (tabled until confirmed).

## 797. K-family 17 registered: political favourites a week before the outcome is known — the underconfidence finding (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any political price is joined to an outcome.** arXiv 2602.19520 (353 M trades): Kalshi
politics is UNDER-confident at nearly every horizon (calibration slope up to 1.83; pooled horizon factor 0.99 at < 1 h → 1.32 beyond a
month); e.g. a 70¢ political contract a week out maps to ≈ 83%. Race markets close at CERTIFICATION, weeks after election night, so
"days before close" is meaningless; the anchor is the price's own resolution.
- **Universe:** settled markets of Elections/Politics series whose tickers are races or nominations (regex `^(KX)?(SENATE|HOUSE|GOV|PRES|
  MAYOR|ECVOTE|POPVOTE|SENATEPARTY|GOVPARTY|PRESPARTY)` or containing `NOM`), volume ≥ 5,000 contracts (`kalshi/k17_politics.py`).
- **Anchor R:** the first day whose daily close is ≥ 0.97 or ≤ 0.03 and stays beyond it to the close. **Entry:** the daily candle 7 days
  before R; spread ≤ 5¢. **Test (one):** favourite_YES — mid in [0.60, 0.95] → buy YES at the ask, taker fee.
- **Unit and clustering:** races resolve together (one national error), so t is computed over **resolution weeks** (mean P&L of the
  week's qualifying markets), not markets.
- **Discovery:** R before 2026-01-01 (2024 cycle, 2025 races). Carried with week-clustered t > 1.96 and mean > 0. **Sealed:** R 2026-01-01
  → 2026-10-20 (2026 primaries and specials, many separate dates), once (seed 797); §664.4; §133 otherwise. The 2026-11-03 general is a
  forward look only after a confirm. Capacity: race-market volume (millions of contracts per major race).

## 804. A99 protocol: does Kalshi's NBA moneyline lag ProphetX's moves? (live, no money) (S10)

**No trial; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any price is recorded.** §803: on NBA lines ProphetX's makers moved before Pinnacle. If they also lead
Kalshi, Kalshi's stale side (deep books) can be taken after a ProphetX move.
- **Recorder** (`sports/a99_pxlead.py`, tonight + following nights, pre-tip only): ProphetX public websocket, NBA moneylines → ProphetX fair =
  proportional devig of the two best back prices (both sides needed); Kalshi KXNBAGAME top of book polled every ~3 s (one listing call).
- **Move:** ProphetX fair changes ≥ 2 points within 60 s. **Opportunity at +3 / +10 / +30 / +60 s:** new ProphetX fair − Kalshi ask − fee
  (up) or Kalshi bid − fair − fee (down).
- **Pass (fixed now):** ≥ 20 moves; median opportunity at +10 s ≥ +1¢ and ≥ 1¢ on ≥ 50% of moves → then a closing-line check (do those
  Kalshi fills beat Pinnacle's close?). Otherwise closed. Trading would need the user's Kalshi API key.

## 805. CORRECTION: Tradeify Select Daily V2 payout rules — the plan's dollar estimates were too high (A100) (S10)

**No trial.** Official help article (help.tradeify.co 12853966, read 2026-10-21) and the user (2026-10-21) for V2 50K accounts (bought
after 2026-09-01): a request is at most **min($1,250, 2 × the profit since the last payout, balance − the $2,100 buffer)**, ≥ $250, and the
profit since the last payout must be > 0 (user's example: at $54k, +$500 today → up to $1,000; +$500 on two days → capped at $1,250).
The A63 simulator's "cap" payout (buffer $2,000, no 2× rule, no minimum) let any payout to $1,250 through above the buffer. New payout kind
"daily" in `reporting/a63_firms.py` (state: balance after the last payout). `reporting/a100_official_payouts.py`, same setup as A85
(5 × 50K, 3 NKD + 2 FDXM, $116, live rules), mean net per 84-session run:

| | model so far | **V2 official** |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 starts (median, P>0, p10) | +$21,306 (+13,186, 95%, +1,290) | **+$11,930 (+7,800, 89%, −147)** |
| 2021-26 (P>0) | +$11,988 (76%) | **+$7,958 (74%)** |
| 2010-20 (P>0) | +$4,791 (72%) | **+$3,391 (68%)** |
| zero edge 2021-26 / 2010-20 | +$4,582 / +$2,692 | **+$4,157 / +$2,431** |
| 2021-26 funded paid / live paid / fees | $10,036 / $7,463 / $5,511 | $9,000 / $4,517 / $5,558 |

The 2× rule slows payouts, so accounts reach the 3-payout live move later — most of the loss is live money. The zero-edge value (the
structural reason the plan pays) drops only ~9%. **Every earlier dollar figure for Select Daily (A60-A92, §625-§770, the launch
checklist, the review prep) used the old payout model and is too high — the 2025-start headline by ~80%.** Plan choices (5 × 50K, mix,
live policy) were not re-solved under V2; that is the next check.

the zero-edge side. What holds: no measurable harm at zero edge, and every stop 0.6-0.9× beat 1.0× in the edge runs (shared paths, so
weak evidence). The 0.7× deployment (§815, user-approved) is kept — no downside found, plausible upside — but treat its "+$8k a run" as
uncertain; the demo/live record decides. The plan's dollar figures carry several-thousand-dollar noise between nearby settings.

## 835. K-family 19 registered: follow LARGE takers in Kalshi's non-sports markets — is the tape's informed flow under-priced? (S10)

**No trial at registration; N 1,539. Written BEFORE any trade is fetched.** Why: §790 found takers informed at every size (makers' markout
negative); §695 found informed sellers fill thin bids at once. If large takers' information is only partly absorbed, copying them from the
public trade tape pays — a structural, public, low-capital rule. Never tested (K14 followed price MOVES in esports, not trades).
- **Universe:** K15's settled non-sports listing (same categories), volume ≥ 5,000 contracts. Random sample (seed 835) of 3,000 discovery
  markets (close 2026-08-14 → 09-20) and 3,000 sealed (09-21 → 10-20). Trades from `/markets/trades` (≤ 20 pages a market).
- **Signal:** the FIRST taker trade in the market whose taker-side notional (count × taker-side price) ≥ $250, taker-side price 10-90¢, more
  than 10 minutes before the close.
- **Entry:** the first trade ≥ 60 s after the signal, at that trade's price for the signal's side + 1¢ slippage + the taker fee; held to
  settlement. One entry per market. Markets without a later trade are skipped.
- **Decision (discovery):** carried if mean P&L per contract > 0 and t over close-days > 1.96. **Sealed:** strict §664.4 (t over days >
  1.645, sign-flip placebo ≥ 95th, posterior > 0 with PRIOR_SD 0.02) → CONFIRM; else WATCHLIST if mean > 0, else REJECT. One trial if
  validated. Reported, not decided on: $1,000 notional threshold; 300 s lag; by category.
- **Amended before any trade is fetched:** rain series (`KXRAIN*`) are dropped from the universe before sampling — the user excludes
  rain markets. Block trades (`is_block_trade`) never count as the signal.

| | 84 sessions 2021-26 | 252 sessions 2021-26 | 84 s 2010-20 | 252 s 2010-20 | zero edge 252 s (21-26 / 10-20) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deployed | +$13,274 (43.6 evals, paid $18.3k) | +$40,960 (117.8 evals) | +$4,306 | +$13,353 | +$5,011 / +$13,430 |
| steady x0.5 | −$2,345 (21.2 evals, paid $109) | −$6,306 | −$2,135 | −$5,549 | −$7,540 / −$5,560 |

Every paired CI is far below zero. Why: NKD's smallest contract is $5 × Nikkei (one-session SD ≈ $2,850) against a $2,000 drawdown, and a
round trip costs ≈ $57; shrinking the brackets shrinks the edge captured per trade but not the cost, so small-bracket trading bleeds to
the drawdown anyway (still 14-55 evaluations a run) and rarely reaches the $3,000 target. The plan's value is the asymmetric bet (loss
capped at $116, payouts kept); in 2010-20 it is ALL structure (+$13.4k with or without the edge). The deployed policy stays.

## 840. V-family 1 protocol — reverse-split round-up arbitrage: a measurement of a structural stream (S11: new arenas)

**No trial (a structural stream measured, like T-family 1 §731). Written BEFORE any price is fetched.** The user (2026-10-21) moved the search
off prediction markets and the Tradeify plan. Mechanism: when a company reverse-splits 1-for-N and rounds fractional holdings UP to a whole
share (some add "round-lot protection": holders of < 100 post-split shares get 100), one pre-split share bought before the effective date
becomes ≥ 1 post-split share. Capacity is one position per brokerage account per event — the "why isn't everyone": many accounts, effort,
broker handling, delayed share credit (~10 trading days).
- **Events:** EDGAR full-text search (8-K, 6-K; 2025-10-01 → 2026-10-21) for "reverse stock split" with "rounded up" / "round up"; per company
  and effective date, the announcing document is parsed for the ratio, effective date, and rounding language. Classes: **holder-level round
  up** (1 share), **round-lot protection** (100 shares), **participant-level / DTC-participant rounding or cash in lieu** (excluded — the
  broker, not the holder, gets it). Unparseable events are listed, not guessed.
- **Per event, per account:** cost = raw close the day before the effective date (1 share); value = shares received × close 10 trading days
  after the effective date (Yahoo daily, split-adjusted, un-adjusted with its split events); no commissions.
- **Read:** qualifying events a month; median and total profit per account a month; dollars a month at 10 and 20 accounts. **A lead** if
  ≥ $2,000 a month at ≤ 20 accounts in both halves of the year (10-2025→03-2026, 04→10-2026) — then broker handling is checked before anything
  else. Otherwise closed.
- **Added before any price is fetched (desk check):** SIFMA's Dec-2025 issuer best practice makes cash-in-lieu the default; the revRSS
  tracker's author stopped in Nov 2024 after manipulation probes (shareholder-count jumps before splits) and retroactive switches from
  round-up to cash-in-lieu that left SHORT positions in traders' accounts; broker handling varies (Fidelity free; some charge $38-50 a
  reorganisation; Robinhood/tastytrade have deposited fractions instead). Even a passing V1 is a lead only after current broker handling
  is confirmed; retroactive-change risk is reported as the share of events whose terms changed after announcement where visible.

## 844. X3 protocol — Coinbase new-listing openings vs Kraken: is there a HEDGED cross-venue gap at the open? (S11)

**No trial (a structural stream measured). Written after a crude screen and BEFORE the contemporaneous measure is computed.** Crude screen
(`xarb/x3_listings.py`, 109 Coinbase USD listings since 2025-03 of assets already on Kraken): Coinbase's first-30-minute VWAP vs Kraken's
last trade BEFORE the open, net of base-tier takers (1.2% + 0.4%), showed +4-27% on several (TRIA, BLEND, UP, ZKP, DRV, PROMPT) — but that
mixes the listing pump (unhedged) with any cross-venue gap. **The tradeable stream:** tokens deposited on Coinbase during its transfer-only
phase are sold at the open while the same amount is bought on Kraken at the same time (inventory unchanged).
- **Measure, per listing:** for each of the first 30 one-minute Coinbase candles with volume: Coinbase close vs Kraken VWAP of the same
  minute (Kraken public trade history; minute skipped if Kraken has no trade). Net gap = Coinbase / Kraken − 1 − 1.6%. Capacity per listing
  = Σ over positive-gap minutes of min(10% of Coinbase minute volume, 10% of Kraken minute volume) × net gap (a 10% participation cap).
- **Read:** listings a month; median and total capturable dollars a month; first and second halves of the sample (to 2025-12-31, from
  2026-01-01). **A lead** if ≥ $2,000 a month in BOTH halves at 10% participation; then the deposit / transfer-only timing and inventory
  price risk are checked before anything else. Otherwise closed.

**No trial.** Resale is legal in Texas with no price cap and starts at one ticket. Data: Ticketmaster Discovery API needs an API key (401),

**A lead** if the volume-tier capacity ≥ $2,000 a month (scaled from the 20 days) AND ≥ $1,000 a month at base tier; then execution realism.

## 852. H-family 1 protocol — after a small-cap LULD pause reopens: continuation or reversal? (S11, new arena: US small caps)

- **Events:** every LUDP pause with a resumption trade time, 09:45-15:30 ET, price ≥ $1. Direction = sign of (last 1-min close before the
  halt − close 5 minutes before that). One event per symbol per day (the first).
- **Rules (4):** at the close of the first full minute after resumption, go WITH the direction or AGAINST it; exit at +15 or +30 minutes'
  close. Cost 1.0% a round trip (small-cap spread + slippage; no commission).
- **Split:** trading days in the window ordered by date; first half discovery, second half sealed. Carry if discovery mean > 0 and t > 1.96
  (clustered by day); sealed: strict §664.4 (t over days > 1.645, sign-flip placebo ≥ 95th, posterior > 0 with PRIOR_SD 0.02 in return
  units) → CONFIRM. Each carried rule validated is a trial.
- **Capacity read** if confirmed: median 1-min dollar volume after resumption.

## 869. D-family 1 protocol — DFS guaranteed-prize overlays on DraftKings: how much free money is left at lock? (S11)

**No trial (a structural stream measured). Written BEFORE any snapshot is taken.** Mechanism: a guaranteed (GPP) contest pays its full
prize pool even when it does not fill; if entries × fee < prize pool at lock, the shortfall ("overlay") is paid by DraftKings to the field.
An average-skill entry then has EV = prize / entries > fee. Classic DFS is legal in Texas and starts at $0.25-$5 entries; "why isn't
everyone": overlays are small, late, and in odd contests. Public lobby (`draftkings.com/lobby/getcontests?sport=…`, no login).
- **Recorder** (`dfs/d1_overlay.py`): every 3 minutes, for NFL / NBA / NHL / NCAAF / MLB / CBB / SOC, all contests with
  `attr.IsGuaranteed` and a cash prize (`pd.Cash`), starting within 45 minutes: id, start, fee, prize, entries, max entries. The last
  snapshot before start is the lock state (DraftKings closes entry at start).
- **Per contest:** overlay $ = max(0, prize − entries × fee); EV ratio = prize / (entries × fee). Fillable room = max − entries.
- **Read after ≥ 3 days covering a weekend:** overlay contests a day; total overlay $ a day; the share of each overlay one person could
  capture at the contest's max-entries-per-user (`mec`, entries × prize / entries); dollars a month for one account entering every overlay
  contest at its per-user cap, assuming field-average results. **A lead** if ≥ $2,000 a month for one account at field-average results (the
  user must then decide on a DraftKings account; skill and lineup tooling come after). Otherwise closed.
- **Amended before any lock readout (2026-10-22 ~14:35 CT):** sports extended to GOLF, MMA, NAS, TEN, LOL, CS, CFL, F1 (niche slates are
  where overlays should live); contests de-duplicated by id; CBB dropped (no such lobby code). Earlier snapshots stand.
- **Readout arithmetic fixed (before any multi-day result):** one account's take = max over k ≤ min(per-user cap, room) of k·prize/(n+k) − k·fee
  (own entries dilute the overlay); the first version overstated it. First slate (UEL soccer 10-22): 9 of 17 guaranteed contests in overlay,
  $322 in total.
- **Caveats fixed now:** (1) Texas legal status is grey — AG Paxton's 2016 opinion (nonbinding) calls paid DFS likely illegal gambling;
  DraftKings kept operating in Texas, FanDuel agreed to leave (2016). The user decides before any account. (2) One account per person at
  DraftKings → no scaling beyond one account. (3) Field-average results assumed; overlay contests may draw strong regulars.
  (4) Ticket/seat-prize contests (~11% of the NFL lobby) are not valued (the lobby gives a ticket count, not its worth) → understates.
  Side screens: FanDuel's lobby API needs a login (401); Splash Sports is mostly pick'em/survivor pools (excluded) with no open lobby.
  Lock state = last snapshot ≤ 10 min before start (contests seen only earlier, e.g. during a recorder restart, are dropped).

## 878. A-LIP2 protocol — shadow competitive quoting on event-settled Kalshi rewards markets (no money) (S10)

**No trial. Written BEFORE any shadow quote is simulated.** §877 showed event-settled series pay rewards without much adverse selection
at the thin-side scale; the allowed series pay ≈ $33,500/day in rewards (2026-10-22), most of it to competitive quoters, not thin sides.
Question: does joining the best bid on BOTH sides earn more in rewards than the quotes lose to the trades that fill them?
- **Universe each cycle (60 s):** active liquidity programmes on `INCLUDE` series (KXTRUTHSOCIAL*, KXRT*, KXRAIN*, *MENTION*), the 40 with
  the highest reward per day (re-ranked hourly). Public endpoints only.
- **Shadow quote:** 100 contracts bid at the best bid on YES and on NO (never crossing). Reward per cycle = side_share (the bot's §694
  formula) × side rate × 60 s for each side, counted only when both sides reach the target with our size included.
- **Fills (conservative queue):** public trades since the last cycle; a YES bid at p fills on taker-NO trades at yes price ≤ p, beyond
  the size resting ahead of us at p (we join last); likewise NO. Filled inventory is held to settlement; quoting continues (a YES fill
  at p and a NO fill at q lock 1 − p − q).
- **Read after ≥ 3 days, per series and in total:** rewards; fill P&L at settlement (unsettled marked at the last mid, reported apart);
  net per day; capital (max simultaneous collateral + inventory). **A lead** if net > 0 in total and in at least two series, with net ≥
  $2,000/month at a capital the user can scale to; then a small live test. Otherwise closed.

## 888. G1 protocol — shadow quoting on Gemini Predictions NFL reward markets (no money; user: test without live funds) (S10)

**No trial. Written before any G1 quote is simulated.** Universe: Pro Football events in `/liquidity-rewards/events` whose game starts
within 5 days, all quarter/half/game markets, first contract of each; a fixed random sample of 60 (seed 888), re-drawn daily from the
list. Every 120 s: book (`/v1/book/{symbol}`) and trades (`/v1/trades/{symbol}`). **Our quote:** 100 contracts bid at mid − 2¢ and ask at
mid + 2¢ (mid = book mid; if a side is empty, the contract's displayed price; skipped if none), never crossing. **Reward per cycle:**
pool/1440 × 2 min × our score / (our score + others'), with score = size / spread² per Gemini's published formula (others: each resting
order within 5¢ of mid scored as size / (2·distance)², floor 1¢); counted only before the game's start time. **Fills:** public trades at or
through our price (we are best when inside the book; otherwise we join last), held to the contract's result. **Read after the 10-25/26 slate
settles:** rewards, fill P&L, net, per market type (quarter/half/full); capital = max simultaneous collateral. Flagged as untestable without
money: actual payment rules (eligibility, per-minute pro-rating, two-sided checks).
- **Started 2026-10-22 22:53Z** (`futres-g1`, until 2026-10-27 06:00Z). First cycle: 52 of 60 sampled markets quotable; simulated
  rewards $3.04 per 2 min (≈ $2,200/day on ≈ $5,200 of quotes) — implausibly high, so fills and the unverifiable payment rules decide.
  Gemini's realised-payout summary (`/liquidity-rewards/summary/daily`) needs an authenticated account (401).

plausible win rate). Otherwise closed.

- **Rule:** buy at the close of the Coinbase 1-minute candle starting 1 minute after the notice (entry lag variants 2 and 5 minutes
  reported only); sell at the close 60 minutes after the notice (15 and 240 minutes reported only). Cost 1.2% round trip (Coinbase taker).
- **Split:** notices before 2026-01-01 discovery, from 2026-01-01 sealed. Carry if discovery mean > 0 and t > 1.96 (one return per event);
  sealed: strict §664.4 (t > 1.645, sign-flip placebo ≥ 95th, posterior > 0 with PRIOR_SD 0.02) → CONFIRM. One trial.
- Delisting / warning notices (shorts) are out of scope (no spot shorting on Coinbase).

## 907. C-family 1 protocol — large hourly moves in liquid crypto (Coinbase USD): reversal or continuation? (S11)

**No trial at registration; N 1,541. Written BEFORE any candle is fetched.** Universe: the 40 Coinbase USD pairs with the most 30-day USD
volume on 2026-10-23 (stablecoins excluded). Data: Coinbase 1-hour candles 2024-01-01 → 2026-10-22. Event: an hour whose close-to-close
return is beyond ±5% or ±8% (first event per coin per 24 h). **Rules (2 directions × 2 thresholds × 3 holds = 12):** reversal (buy after a

> 0 and t (clustered by event day) > 1.96; sealed strict §664.4 → CONFIRM, one trial per carried rule.

## 964. AU-family 1 protocol — paid smart-contract audit contests (Sherlock, Cantina): flow first, then a blind shadow audit (S11)

**No trial (a measurement). Written before any contest's results are read.** A new arena: crowdsourced security-audit contests pay USDC
prize pools for valid High/Medium findings in published code. It is effort work (code review, which Claude does), not trading, so none of
the trading exclusions apply. Code4rena reportedly closed 2026-05-13 (one source); Sherlock (`audits.sherlock.xyz/api/contests`) and
Cantina (`cantina.xyz/api/v0/competitions`) have public APIs.
1. **Flow (stage 1):** contests ending 2026-04-01 → 2026-10-24 on both platforms: count, prize pools (bug-bounty programmes kept separate),
   participants and per-researcher payouts where published. **Pass:** ≥ $300k a month of contest pools AND a typical contest pays its
   10th-ranked researcher ≥ $500. Eligibility (US / Texas, KYC, payment) checked from the platforms' terms.
2. **Shadow audit (stage 2, only if stage 1 passes):** pick finished contests that started after 2026-06-30 (after Claude's training cutoff;
   no leakage from published reports), audit the in-scope code blind (results not read until the audit is written and saved with a hash),
   then score each claimed finding against the judged list; payout = what the platform's formula would have paid. **Pass:** ≥ 1 valid
   High/Medium in at least half the contests audited and a simulated payout ≥ $1,000 a month at a feasible pace (≤ 2 contests a week).

## 966. X-family 1 protocol — buying straddles into earnings (the pre-announcement IV run-up; Gao, Xing & Zhang 2018), on real bid/ask (S11)

**Written before any option price is read.** Data: DoltHub `post-no-preference/options` (`option_chain`: end-of-day bid/ask/delta, about
three snapshots a week, three expirations, US stocks; 2020 → 2026-10); earnings dates from the Nasdaq calendar (as in E2). Mechanism
(published): implied volatility rises into a known announcement by more than it costs to hold, because demand for event exposure arrives late.
1. **Events:** announcement date d with calendar market cap ≥ $10B, 2020-01-01 → 2026-10-16, one per symbol per d.
2. **Exit snapshot X:** the latest snapshot date ≤ d − 1 trading day and ≥ d − 4 calendar days (the timing field is mostly missing, so the exit
   is always before even a pre-market report). **Entry snapshot E:** the latest snapshot ≤ X − 4 calendar days and ≥ X − 8.
3. **Contract:** the nearest expiration after d present at both snapshots; the strike whose call delta at E is closest to 0.50. **Buy the call +
   put at the ask at E, sell both at the bid at X**; commission $0.65 a contract a leg each way. Return = (bids_X − asks_E − 0.026) / (asks_E +
   0.013). Events with a missing quote or zero bid at X are counted at −100% (the conservative case), and no other events are dropped.
4. **Statistic:** the mean return per event, aggregated into calendar weeks (weekly mean; t on weeks). **Discovery 2020-01 → 2023-12**: carry
   if mean > 0 and t > 1.96. **Sealed 2024-01 → 2026-10**: the §664.4 rule (t > 1.645, sign-flip placebo ≥ 95th, positive posterior with
   PRIOR_SD 0.02). One rule, one trial if carried. Mid-to-mid returns printed for information only.

## 967. X-family 1 clarification and X-family 2 protocol — the opposite trade: a defined-risk short iron fly held through the report (S11)

**Written before any option price is read.** (a) X1 clarification: an event with no expiry spanning the report, or no ask on either leg, *at
entry* is not tradable under the rule and is left out (counted and printed); only exit-side gaps are counted at −100%, as §966.3 says.
(b) **X2 (one rule):** the variance premium may sit in the event itself (IV overprices the earnings move), and a small account can only sell it with
defined risk. Same events, same expiration choice. At **X** (§966.2, the last snapshot before the report): **sell** the call and put at the strike
with call delta closest to 0.50 at the bid; **buy** the call whose delta is closest to +0.20 and the put whose delta is closest to −0.20 at the ask
(those strikes need to be at least one strike away from the body, otherwise the event is untradable). **Exit Y:** the first snapshot ≥ d + 1 calendar day and
≤ d + 5 calendar days; buy the body back at the ask, sell the wings at the bid; a leg without a quote at Y is valued at intrinsic from that
day's Yahoo close (the body at intrinsic + 2% of the price, the wings at intrinsic). Commission $0.65 a contract a leg each way. **Return on
risk** = P&L / (max loss = wider wing − net credit); an event with no Y snapshot is untradable. Statistic, windows and the §664.4 rule as X1;
one trial if carried.

## 968. Screen: Metaculus FutureEval bot tournaments — no capital at risk, ~$200k a year to ~110 eligible bots; needs the user's account — PARKED as a lead (S11)

**No trial (a desk screen).** Not a market: bots post forecasts on 300-400 questions a season and prizes go to the best sum of peer scores.
**Pools:** Spring, Summer and Fall 2026 seasons at $50-58k each (Fall: questions 2026-09-28 → 2027-01-06; joining open until a few weeks
before 2027-01-01, late joiners start at 0 points, so a late start forfeits the missed questions), plus MiniBench ($1,000 per two-week round of
~60 auto-generated questions) and the Metaculus Cup ($5k; a bot won Summer 2026). **Payouts (published tables):** Q2 2025 ($30k, 96 bots):
#1 $7,550, #2 $4,563, #3 $3,270, #9 $1,731, #20 $465; Q1 2025: #10 $2,228. **Spring 2026:** 173 bots (111 eligible); the best single-prompt
baseline (GPT-5.1 high + AskNews) placed 18th; the top bots ensemble several frontier models with multi-source research (AskNews, Perplexity),
take the median and aggregate several runs; 7 of the top 10 makers were hobbyists. **What it would earn:** a baseline-plus bot ≈ #10-20 ≈
$0.5-2k a season; top 3 ≈ $5-10k a season — i.e. ≈ $150-700/month typical, ~$2k/month only at the top, capped by rank (one bot each), not by
capital. **Costs:** LLM calls (~$100-500 a season; Metaculus grants sponsor credits selectively) and a free AskNews account. **Blocked on the
user:** a Metaculus account + bot account + participation form (the API refuses unauthenticated calls, Cloudflare blocks the site). No
measurement possible until then; a backtest would score our bot on Summer-2026 questions (post-cutoff) against the published leaderboard.
Parked; to be put to the user with the next report.

## 969. X-family 3 protocol — cheap volatility: buy straddles where realised volatility exceeds implied (Goyal & Saretto 2009), real bid/ask (S11)

**Written before any option price is read.** Published: sorting stocks on HV − IV, the high-HV/low-IV decile's straddles earned large monthly
returns in 1996-2006 (mean reversion of the mis-estimated volatility). Untested after publication on real quotes here; small accounts can only
buy (defined risk), so one long-only rule.
1. **Formation:** the first DoltHub snapshot of each month, 2020-02 → 2026-09. Per symbol: the expiration 20-45 calendar days out (nearest to
   30 if two); ATM strike = call delta nearest 0.50 (fetched with |delta| in 0.35-0.65); **IV** = mean of that strike's call and put `vol`;
   **HV** = annualised s.d. of the last 21 daily log returns from `data/stocks/long/pack.npz` (symbols present there only, ≥ 250 days of
   history, strike ≥ $10, both legs with a positive bid and ask, relative spread of the straddle ≤ 20% of its mid).
2. **Rule:** buy the straddle (call + put at the ask, $0.65 a contract a leg) on the top decile of log(HV / IV), equal weight. **Exit:** the last
   snapshot ≥ 3 calendar days before the expiration, both legs at the bid (fetched with no delta filter); a leg with no bid there counts as 0.
3. **Statistic:** the monthly equal-weight mean return on premium; t on months. **Discovery 2020-02 → 2023-12** (carry: mean > 0, t > 1.96);
   **sealed 2024-01 → 2026-09** under §664.4. One rule, one trial if carried.

## 970. Screen: WorldQuant BRAIN consultant programme — paid per alpha, no capital, US eligible; pay unpublished; needs the user's account — PARKED as a lead (S11)

**No trial (a desk screen).** BRAIN users write alpha expressions and run them in WorldQuant's simulator (their data); users who reach Gold
(10,000 points) may be invited as Research Consultants, paid a base fee per period that depends on the quantity and quality of submitted alphas and
on their correlation with WorldQuant's existing pool. Nothing is paid in a month without a qualifying submission. **Pay:** WorldQuant advertises
≈ $8,000+/quarter (Grandmaster) and $2,000+ (Master) at the top two levels. 2022 regional fee documents (copies only) cap the top tier at $3,500 a month.
Typical earnings are unpublished and reported as modest. **US:** listed among 17 eligible regions. **Automation:** Python API access is a listed
consultant feature, and open-source LLM alpha agents exist (wq-alpha-agent and others), so machine-generated alphas already crowd the pool;
the correlation penalty is what limits pay. **What it needs:** the user's BRAIN account (free) and the consultant contract (identity, tax);
no measurement is possible before that, since the simulator is behind the login. Plausibly a few hundred dollars a month, more only at the
top levels; capped by quality, not capital. Parked with §968, to put to the user.

## 974. X-family 4 protocol — SPY put credit spreads, monthly (the index variance premium with defined risk) (S11)

**Written before any SPY option price is read.** The best-documented option premium is that index puts are overpriced. A small account can
sell it only with defined risk. **Rule (one):** at the first DoltHub snapshot of each month, 2020-02 → 2026-09, take the SPY expiration 20-45 calendar
days out (nearest 30). **Sell** the put with delta nearest −0.30 at the bid and **buy** the put with delta nearest −0.15 at the ask (the strikes
must differ), $0.65 a contract a leg. **Exit:** the last snapshot ≥ 3 calendar days before the expiration; buy back the short at the ask and sell
the long at the bid (a leg with no quote is valued at intrinsic from that day's SPY close in `data/stocks/y_SPY.json`, plus 1% of the price on the
short). **Return on risk** = P&L / (width − credit). Statistic: the monthly return on risk. Discovery 2020-02 → 2023-12 (carry: mean > 0,
t > 1.96); sealed 2024-01 → 2026-09 under §664.4.

## 975. X-family amendment (data structure, before any return was read): DoltHub lists only three target expirations per snapshot (S11)

**No trial.** Found while debugging X4's empty exits (every exit query returned no rows; no P&L was looked at, and the X4 run printed a
number built on intrinsic-only exits, which is void and not used). Each snapshot carries just three expirations, chosen relative to that
date: ≈ 2 weeks, ≈ 4 weeks and a month-end/monthly one (e.g. 2023-12-18: 12-29, 01-12, 02-16; 2023-12-27: 01-09, 01-26, 02-16). A
given expiry is therefore listed on some snapshots only, and never in its last ~10 days. The rules are amended as follows:
- **X1:** the expiration is the nearest one after d that is listed at **both** E and X. A leg missing from X's delta-filtered pull is fetched
  exactly (strike + expiry) before scoring; only a leg still unquoted counts at −100%.
- **X2:** the expiration is the nearest one after d listed at both X and Y (Y's pull takes all listed expirations).
- **X3 and X4:** the exit is the **last snapshot ≤ expiry − 3 days on which that expiry is listed** (searching back from expiry − 3 for up to
  six snapshots). If none is found, the trade is untradable and counted.
Everything else stands as registered.

## 976. X-family amendment 2 (data structure): the strike grid is sparse and moves, so unlisted exit legs are valued from that day's IV smile (S11)

**No trial.** X4's re-run (−31.9%/month, t −5.15) is **void**. 67 of its 90 exit legs fell back to intrinsic + 1% because the snapshot lists ≈ 25
strikes spread over a wide range (spacing ≈ $10 on SPY), and that set changes from date to date. The exact traded strike is usually absent at
exit (e.g. short 287 / long 278 entered 2020-03-02; listed 03-16 strikes 205-276, neither present). Any rule that holds a contract
and exits it therefore needs a valuation for unlisted legs. **Amendment, all X rules, before any return is read:** a leg listed at exit trades
at its own bid/ask. An unlisted leg is valued with Black-76 on the forward **F = K* + C* − P*** (mid prices at the listed strike K* with call delta
nearest 0.50, same expiry and date), T = days to expiry / 365, r = 0, and σ interpolated linearly in strike between the two nearest listed
strikes of the same type (flat beyond the listed range). Its bid/ask = model price × (1 ∓ half the relative spread of the nearest listed
strike of that type). The −100% / intrinsic fallbacks then apply only when the expiry itself is unlisted at exit, or no IV is available.

## 977. X-family 4: SPY put credit spreads lose after real spreads — −11.2% a month on risk, t −1.85; not carried (S11)

**N 1,554 (no trial).** `src/futuresres/options/x4_spyputs.py` (exits valued per §975/§976; 0 intrinsic fallbacks). Discovery 2020-02 →
2023-12: 45 months (2 untradable), mean −11.17% on risk a month, t −1.85, 62% winners, worst −113%. Spot checks look right: 2020-09
S 358 → 339 cost 5.51 to close a 1.66 credit; quiet months keep 70-90% of the credit. The index variance premium does not survive the
bid/ask of a two-leg spread closed early, and the losses in 2020 and 2022 dominate. Closed.

## 978. X-family 1: the pre-earnings IV run-up is +1.5% an event at mid — far below the spread; −16% at bid/ask, t −22; not carried (S11)

**N 1,554 (no trial).** `src/futuresres/options/x1_straddle.py` (§966, §975, §976). Discovery 2020-2023: 7,439 tradable events (5,546
untradable: no expiry spanning the report listed at both snapshots, or no entry quote), 198 weeks. **Net (ask in, bid out) −16.26% an
event-week, t −22.10, 12% winners.** −100% fallbacks are only 0.7%. The loss is the quoted spread: DoltHub's end-of-day straddle spread has a
median of **12.5% of the straddle** (10th-90th percentile 4.5%-53%), wider than intraday markets in large caps. Mid-to-mid, the published
run-up is present but small: **+1.5% an event** (excluding fallbacks), below even a realistic 2-3% round-trip spread on a
large-cap straddle. Not carried on either reading. Note for X2/X3: with spreads this wide in the data, a rule needs a gross edge well above 10%
a trade to carry. Mid-to-mid figures are printed alongside for information.

## 979. B-family 3 protocol — Expensify open-source bounties ($175-250 an issue via Upwork): flow, competition, and the rules (S11)

**No trial (a measurement). Written before any issue's comments are read.** Expensify/App labels paid issues "External" with a price in
the title (2026-07-01 → 10-23: 1,183 such issues; 2026-H1: 2,275). Contributors post proposals; a reviewer picks one, who opens the PR and
is paid via Upwork after merge plus a regression period. **Measure** on External issues created 2026-08-01 → 09-30 that are closed: proposals per issue
(comments with a "Proposal" heading), minutes from the "Help Wanted" label to the first proposal, the share of issues won by the top 10
and top 50 assignees, and the price. Also read CONTRIBUTING / the bounty rules (AI use, eligibility, payment, limits on concurrent
assignments). **Pass:** a newcomer can plausibly win ≥ 10 issues a month (≈ $1,750) — i.e. winners are not concentrated in a closed
group, proposals per issue ≤ ~10, and the rules allow AI-assisted work; if passed, a stage 2 would be the user's call (it needs their GitHub +
Upwork accounts).

## 980. B-family 3: Expensify's own AI agent takes most jobs — outside contributors are paid on ~1 in 4 paid issues, ≈ $12k a month for all of them combined; closed (S11)

**No trial (a measurement).** `data/bounty/expensify_*.json` (GitHub API). 469 External issues were created 2026-08/09 and are now closed (≈ 235 a month).
In a random 80 (seed 979), **MelvinBot** (Expensify's agent, first proposal by design) proposed on 53. The median issue drew 1 proposal (mean 2.6).
Of the 55 with a payment summary, **15 paid an outside contributor** (typically $250; one $750, one $500); the rest paid only the C+ reviewer,
i.e. Melvin's fix was used. Scaled up: ≈ 44 outside-contributor jobs a month, ≈ $12k a month split among ~46 active proposers. The top
three took 11 of the 15. The rules make it worse for a newcomer: one job at a time until the first PR merges; outside proposals must be "meaningfully different"
from Melvin's; every PR must be tested on web, iOS, Android and desktop (this laptop cannot build the app); a 50% penalty per regression.
A newcomer would plausibly win a few jobs a month, far from the bar. Closed.

## 990. L-family 18 protocol — closed-end fund discount reversion, reopened (§918's data blocker is gone: Yahoo serves CEF NAVs as X{ticker}X) (S11)

**Written before any NAV or return is read.** Universe: listed tickers from the Nasdaq screener cache (`data/stocks/screener.json`) whose
name contains Fund / Trust / Income / Municipal / Opportunit / Strategic and whose Yahoo NAV symbol X{ticker}X exists with
instrumentType MUTUALFUND. Daily close (raw) and adjusted close from Yahoo for price, NAV close for the NAV. **Signal at each month-end:**
discount D = price / NAV − 1; z = (D − its 252-session mean) / its 252-session s.d. (≥ 200 valid days; NAV and price dated the same
session). **Rule (one):** buy the 10 lowest-z funds (discounts unusually wide versus their own history) at the month-end close, hold one month on
adjusted close (distributions included), minus the equal-weight universe the same month, minus 0.4% cost. **Statistic:** monthly excess; t
on months. Discovery 2013-06 → 2021-12 (carry: mean > 0, t > 1.96); sealed 2022-01 → 2026-09 under §664.4. Year-round, liquid listed
funds, cash account.

## 999. Screen: sports-betting prop firms (simulated bankrolls, paid challenges) — small, unproven counterparties; closed (S11)

**No trial (a desk screen).** These are the sports analogue of the Tradeify plan: buy a challenge on a simulated bankroll and earn a profit split once
funded. Current operators (comparison checked 2026-10-03): Prime Sports Funded (€109 for €5k, +35% in ≥ 25 picks, 2-5% stakes, 20% max
loss, 80% split), Fan Funded ($59.99, three +33% steps), GetBet Funded, Bankroll U (US-only, $245), Playvo, OddsON, MySportsFunding (€499
instant). Against the user's criteria: **no published payout proof**, mostly euro-priced small operators, and churn (Funded Sports Trader closed,
Funded Stake offline, BETfunded stopped selling, Player Profit absorbed). Texas status is unstated, and sports wagering is illegal in Texas.
Desk EV at −110 odds with no edge: pass ≈ 25% (drift −0.2% a 5% bet across ~28 bets) against a €109 fee and a capped split. Roughly break-even
before counterparty risk, and positive only with a real pick edge, which §677/§687 did not find. Closed; not a legitimate-KYC venue in the user's sense.

## 1011. AI-family 1 protocol — Claude reads earnings releases blind; buy the next open on strong positive reads (Lopez-Lira & Tang 2023), post-cutoff only (S11)

**Written before any filing is read or any price is looked up.** The edge would be Claude's reading. No leakage is possible because every event is
after the model's training cutoff (June 2026). **Events:** 8-K filings with Item 2.02 ("Results of Operations and Financial Condition") filed
2026-07-01 → 2026-10-16 by companies in `pack.npz`, accepted outside regular hours (16:00-23:59 ET → trade the next session; 00:00-09:29 ET → trade
that session). A random sample of **300** (seed 1011), drawn from the event list before any text is read. **Scoring (blind):** Claude reads the
EX-99.1 press release text only (no prices, no headlines from other sources, no web search) and writes a score −2…+2 for the expected
next-day stock reaction *beyond what an average release implies* (guidance, beats or misses stated in the text, tone), saved with a hash
before any price is fetched. **Rule (one, long-only):** buy at the open of the trade session when score ≥ +1, sell at that close; return
minus SPY's open→close the same session, minus 0.1%. **Statistic:** mean excess over the ≥ +1 events, t; and, for information, the Spearman
correlation of score with excess across all 300. **Decision:** this is a single sealed sample (no discovery split, since post-cutoff data is
scarce). Under the §664.4 rule (t > 1.645, placebo ≥ 95th, posterior > 0) → CONFIRM / WATCHLIST / REJECT. One trial.

## 1012. AI-1 scores frozen before any price is read — sha256 0482669d8b7ec19f5c5f01f5ef597ec8a96fb5e3bdcbfd5a8c000fcdfe2a746f (S11)

**No trial yet.** 1,703 after-hours Item 2.02 8-Ks; a 300 sample (seed 1011). 298 had text: 228 via the EX-99 regex, 70 via a fallback fixed before
reading (the largest non-8-K .htm). Some fallbacks are cover pages or supplements, scored 0. Claude read the first ≈ 2,200 characters of each
(headline, results, guidance) with no prices, headlines or search, in batches of 15. Scores: +2 59, +1 109, 0 104, −1 17, −2 9. The rule's long
set (≥ +1) is 168 events. Heuristic used throughout: raised/beat guidance → +1/+2; reaffirmed or no information → 0; lowered guidance or misses → −1/−2.
`data/ai1/scores.json` (sorted keys) hashes to the value above, and `ai1_reads score` refuses to run if the file changes.

## 1013. AI-1: Claude's blind reads of earnings releases do not predict the post-open move — +0.02%/trade, t 0.05, Spearman −0.035; WATCHLIST in name only (t01556); N → 1,556 (S11)

**Trial t01556.** 299 scored lines (Z and ZG share one release), 169 longs (score ≥ +1): mean open→close excess over SPY after 0.1% =
**+0.02%, t +0.05, placebo 52nd, posterior +0.02% → WATCHLIST** under §664.4 (positive mean), but it is a null in substance. By score: −2 −1.35%
(n 9), −1 +0.54% (17), 0 +0.50% (104), +1 +0.02% (110), +2 +0.04% (59). Rank correlation of score with excess across all: −0.035. The
information in the release is in the opening print, and what Claude reads adds nothing to the open→close drift. (Lopez-Lira & Tang's effect
came from headlines and partly from small caps, under different timing.) Closed as a strategy. Nothing here supports an LLM-reading edge for a
retail trader who acts at the open.

## 1014. L-family 23 protocol — earnings-gap continuation: buy the open after a ≥ 4% gap-up on an outside-hours earnings 8-K, sell the close (S11)

**Written before any return is computed.** Events: Item 2.02 8-Ks from EDGAR submissions (exact acceptance times) for `pack.npz` companies,
2016-01 → 2026-10-16, accepted outside regular hours (trade session = next session if after 16:00 ET, same session if before 09:30).
Gap = adjusted open(trade session) ÷ adjusted close(previous session) − 1. **Rule (one, long-only):** gap ≥ +4% → buy the open, sell that
close; return minus SPY open→close the same session, minus 0.1%. One event per company per trade session. **Statistic:** monthly mean, t on
months. Discovery 2016-01 → 2022-12 (carry: mean > 0, t > 1.96); sealed 2023-01 → 2026-10 under §664.4.

## 1015. L-family 23: no earnings-gap continuation intraday — 6,013 gap-ups ≥ 4%, +0.00% a trade, t −0.53; not carried. L24/L25 protocols on the same events (S11)

**N 1,556 (no trial).** `src/futuresres/stocks/l23_gapcont.py`; 63,619 outside-hours Item 2.02 8-Ks (2016-2026) for `pack.npz` names, with exact
acceptance times (`data/stocks/l23/events.json`). Discovery 2016-2022: open→close excess over SPY after 0.1% = −0.065% a trade-month, t −0.53,
47% winners. Closed. **Registered before computing, on the same events and windows (each a trial if carried):**
- **L24 gap-down reversal:** gap ≤ −8% → buy the open, sell that close (minus SPY, 0.1%).
- **L25 gap-up drift:** gap ≥ +4% → buy the open, sell the close 20 sessions later (minus SPY over the same span, 0.2%).

## 1016. L24 gap-down reversal not carried (+0.23%, t 0.86); L25 gap-up 20-session drift a near miss (+0.81% a trade-month, t 1.84) — forward watchlist (S11)

**N 1,556 (no trial).** Discovery 2016-2022 (`l23_gapcont.py L24|L25`). **L24:** 1,871 gap-downs ≤ −8%, open→close +0.227% a trade-month after
costs, t +0.86, 51% winners. Closed. **L25:** 6,013 gap-ups ≥ +4%, open → close 20 sessions later minus SPY minus 0.2% = **+0.809% a
trade-month, t +1.84** (per-trade mean +1.10%, 51% winners). This is the earnings-gap form of post-announcement drift. It sits under the bar, so the sealed
window stays closed, and it goes to the forward watchlist: re-run after a year of new data (2027-10, events refetched). Capital-bound either way (≈ +1% per 20-day
trade, ~70 trades a month across all names).

## 1017. D1 readout of the paused recorder: one afternoon, $402 overlay, ≈ $28 a day for one field-average account; a full week is scheduled (S11)

**No trial.** `python -m futuresres.dfs.d1_overlay` on `data/dfs/d1.jsonl` (96 snapshots, 2026-10-22 only, paused for memory): 28 guaranteed
contests at lock, 16 with overlay, $402 in total. Dominated by one UEL soccer slate ($120 + $65 + $60 + $25 + $26). Golf showdowns had $30 and $20 overlays,
Madden $14. One account at its per-user cap at field-average skill ≈ $28 that day, i.e. ≈ $840 a month if every day looked like this. That's under the
$2k bar and resting on one day. Last snapshots were 0-6 minutes before lock, so late entries may still fill part of it. **Decision:** run the
recorder for a full week (incl. NFL Sunday) once the A-LIP shadows finish, to stay within 3 runs: timer `futres-d1-start` at 2026-10-26 01:30Z,
recorder until 2026-11-02 06:00Z. Readout then. Lead if ≥ $2k/month at field-average with one account (§869).

## 1018. K-calendar 8 protocol — the month-end extension (§961/§963) in other bond ETFs: EDV, ZROZ, MBB, TIP, MUB, HYG, EMB (S11)

**Written before any of these series is read.** Same rule as K5 (§962): buy the close 4 sessions before the last session of the month, sell the last
close; return minus the series' own average 4-session drift, minus 0.02% (0.05% for HYG and EMB, which have wider spreads). Yahoo adjusted closes. Discovery:
months before 2016-01 (each series from its inception); sealed 2016-01 → 2026-09 under §664.4. Each series is its own trial if carried. The point
is scale: EDV/ZROZ carry ≈ 1.4× TLT's duration, so the same flow yields more per dollar without leverage decay.

## 1019. K-calendar 8: the month-end extension CONFIRMED in MBB (t01559) and TIP (t01560); EDV, ZROZ, EMB WATCHLIST; N → 1,561 (S11)

**Trials t01557-t01561.** Discovery (to 2015) carried EDV +0.662% (t 2.13), ZROZ +0.722% (2.34), MBB +0.100% (2.81), TIP +0.177% (2.70), EMB
+0.371% (2.15). Not carried: MUB +0.085% (1.15), HYG +0.135% (0.83). **Sealed 2016-01 → 2026-09 (129 month-ends each):** **MBB +0.130%, t 3.07,
placebo 100th → CONFIRM; TIP +0.133%, t 2.59, placebo 100th → CONFIRM**; EDV +0.270% (t 1.55, 94th), ZROZ +0.312% (t 1.59, 94th), EMB
+0.016% (t 0.20) → WATCHLIST. The index-extension flow is now confirmed in five ETFs (TLT, IEF, LQD, MBB, TIP). It is one mechanism, and the
series are highly correlated (same rate factor), so they do not diversify each other. The largest per-dollar version is the long-duration
EDV/ZROZ (+0.27-0.31% a window, sealed, not significant alone). Dollar scale is unchanged: ≈ $27-31 a month per $10k in EDV, ≈ $65 in TMF.
Still a capital-bound edge, not a $2k/month stream.

## 1020. L-family 26 protocol — quarter-end window dressing: buy the top-20 year-to-date winners 5 sessions before quarter-end (S11)

**Written before any return is computed.** `pack.npz`, price ≥ $5, ≤ 5% missing in the year. At the close 5 sessions before the last session of
March, June, September and December, rank by return since the last close of the prior year (for Q1: the prior 63 sessions). **Rule:** buy the top 20,
sell at the quarter's last close. Return minus the equal-weight universe over the same 5 sessions, minus 0.2%. Discovery quarters before 2023-01;
sealed 2023-01 → 2026-09 under §664.4. One rule.

## 1021. L-family 26: quarter-end window dressing is a near miss — +1.57% per 5-session window, t 1.68, 28 quarters; not carried, forward watchlist (S11)

**N 1,561 (no trial).** `src/futuresres/stocks/l26_window.py`, discovery 2016-2022. A large point estimate on a noisy, high-volatility basket
(YTD winners) with only 28 observations. It goes on the forward watchlist and is re-read with the sealed quarters once a year of new data accrues (the sealed window
stays closed; four quarter-ends a year makes a fair forward test slow).

## 1022. K-calendar 9 protocol — month-end extension in long corporates and international bonds: VCLT, BNDX, IGOV (S11)

**Written before these series are read.** K5's rule and costs (0.02%; IGOV 0.05%). Discovery before 2016-01 (BNDX from 2013); sealed 2016-01 →
2026-09. Each series is a trial if carried. VCLT tests a longer-duration corporate version of LQD's confirmed effect; BNDX/IGOV test whether the
flow exists in non-US index funds.

## 1023. K-calendar 9: VCLT month-end WATCHLIST (t01562; sealed +0.13%, t 1.37); BNDX and IGOV not carried; N → 1,562 (S11)

**Trial t01562.** Discovery: VCLT +0.311% (t 2.36), carried; BNDX +0.083% (t 1.48, 31 months) and IGOV +0.112% (t 1.01) not carried. VCLT sealed
2016-2026: +0.134%, t 1.37, placebo 91st → WATCHLIST. The flow is clearest in US Treasury, MBS, TIPS and IG indices (§1019), weaker in long
corporates and absent from non-US index funds. Closed as a family; nothing changes the capital-bound verdict.

## 1024. New rule and an automation screen of the candidate stack (user, 2026-10-24/25) (S11)

**No trial.** User rules (2026-10-24): small streams may count if their **combined** verified total exceeds **$2k/month**, and **every stream must be
fully automatable** (no daily manual work). Screen of what we have:
- **DFS overlays (D1):** DraftKings' Terms of Use prohibit outside automated tools or scripts for creating, entering or withdrawing from contests and
  managing lineups (policy since 2016). Not automatable, so it does not count. The scheduled week of recording is cancelled to free a run slot
  (`futres-d1-start` and `futres-d1-readout` timers stopped).
- **Reverse-split round-ups (§843, ~$40-70 a month per account):** automation needs a broker API and holder-level round-up handling. Alpaca (API) deposits fractional
  shares and never rounds up (revRSS broker notes; one 2023 note says otherwise, superseded). Tradier (API) credits round-ups at $1.45 an event.
  tastytrade (API) is on-and-off fractional. Schwab, E*TRADE, Public and Webull (APIs) have unknown handling. Brokers also terminate round-up accounts
  (Ally, and Fidelity is a stated risk). Issuers increasingly round at the record-holder level or pay cash (SIFMA default). Automatable portion
  ≈ $100-300 a month with 2-4 API brokers, if handling holds. Counts, but small.
- **Bond month-end (§961-§1019):** automatable through any API broker (scheduled orders). Capital-bound: ≈ $2-6 a month on $200.
- **Metaculus bots (§968/§984):** automatable by design (bot posts forecasts); $0-500 a season typical, more only near the top; needs your accounts.
- Odd-lot tenders, PATROLL, hackathons, freelancing, WorldQuant consultant work: manual, do not count.
**Implication:** the automatable stack today is a few hundred dollars a month, far from $2k. Streams that don't grow with capital and can be automated are scarce once
liquidity rewards and prediction markets are excluded. Search target from here: automatable, capital-light streams.

## 1025. Screens for automatable, capital-light streams (2026-10-25 morning): AI stock imagery, CrunchDAO, equity intraday data — closed or blocked (S11)

**No trial.** (1) **Adobe Stock AI images:** almost half the library is already AI-generated (PetaPixel 2025); per-contributor upload limits since May 2025 depend on past
sales and acceptance; vendor-claimed $0.25-0.50 a download. Saturated and capped, closed. (2) **CrunchDAO / DataCrunch:** rewards in the CRUNCH token on
Solana, a crypto counterparty without the KYC'd-firm standard. Closed. (3) **Intraday US equity data** for capacity-limited small-cap intraday rules: this
repo holds only Databento FTP batch credentials, so pricing or downloading equity data needs the user. Free alternatives: Yahoo (5-minute bars for 60 days,
hourly for 2 years), and Alpaca's free market-data plan (historical bars with an account, which is also the natural automation rail). Blocked on an
account. (4) **Metaculus:** Metaculus's analysis repo has no question or forecast data, so a bot can only be measured by entering it; MiniBench's two-week
rounds are the fastest real test. Prizes are concentrated at the top (Metaculus weighed score-squared and exponential splits to avoid flat payouts).

## 1026. Tradeify allows personal bots — the existing plan can become the automated core once API access exists (S11)

**No trial.** Tradeify's help-centre "Guidelines for traders" (fetched 2026-10-25, "updated over a week ago"): **personal bots are allowed unless they are HFT**.
Conditions: you must prove you are the sole owner; Tradeify may require a live video of you enabling the code on your own PC (so the bot should run on your
machine, not only the droplet); using the same bot at other firms is prohibited; funded payouts need > 50% of trades and > 50% of profit from holds over 10 seconds
(the NKD rule's holds are minutes to hours). Connections: Tradovate, Rithmic or WealthCharts, fixed at purchase (vendor blogs). The binding
constraint stays the one you reported on 10-15: no API order placement until the account reaches the live stage. Until then, staged bracket orders
(§581) are the semi-automated path. For the combined-stack rule, the Tradeify plan is the only scalable automatable piece found so far (prop capital supplies the scale).
